name: Capel Sound
description: Local taxi and wheelchair taxi in Capel Sound (Rosebud West), 24/7. Trips to Rosebud Hospital, Frankston, Melbourne Airport and beyond.
intro: Capel Sound (the area many people still call Rosebud West) sits on the bay between Rosebud and Tootgarook, and Taxi Peninsula covers it at any hour of the day or night. We send a sedan for quick runs to the shops or a friend’s place, and a wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT when a passenger needs to stay seated in their chair. Booking online takes about two minutes, and you’ll get a confirmation by SMS or email.

Most of Capel Sound is quiet residential streets running back from Point Nepean Road, with the foreshore reserve on the bay side filling up with campers and day-trippers every summer. For everyday errands, locals tend to head east into Rosebud for the supermarkets, Rosebud Plaza and the many medical clinics, while Rosebud Hospital is only a short ride away. Specialist appointments often mean Frankston Hospital, and the nearby Mornington Peninsula Freeway makes Capel Sound a straightforward starting point for Melbourne Airport, the city or Southern Cross Station.

If you have an early flight or a morning appointment, book the night before so the trip is locked in. Families heading out together, or a group with a wheelchair user and a few friends, can ask for the Maxi WAT. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers travel with the passenger, so mention them when you book and we’ll make sure everyone fits.
local: Point Nepean Road is the spine of Capel Sound, carrying buses and most local traffic along the bay, while the freeway sits a little inland. Summer is a different story: from Christmas through the school holidays the foreshore camping grounds are full and the bay road slows down, especially on warm weekends. Many streets back from the water look alike and some houses sit behind units or on battle-axe blocks, so give us the cross street or a landmark when you book. If you’re being collected from the foreshore, tell us which section or the nearest beach access point, and the driver will meet you there rather than searching along the reserve.

faq.q: Is Capel Sound the same place as Rosebud West?
faq.a: Yes, Capel Sound is the area that many locals and longtime visitors still call Rosebud West. You can use either name when you book. What matters most is the street address and, if possible, the nearest cross street, so the driver can come straight to your door without circling the backstreets off Point Nepean Road.

faq.q: Can you take me to Rosebud Hospital and bring me home afterwards?
faq.a: Yes. We’ll drop you at the hospital and, if you don’t know when you’ll be finished, choose the “pick up when ready” option. When you’re done, tap “I’m ready” or call us and a car will be on its way. This works well for day procedures, outpatient clinics and discharges where the timing is hard to predict.

faq.q: Can you collect me from the foreshore camping area in summer?
faq.a: Yes, we pick up campers along the Capel Sound foreshore. The reserve is long and gets very busy over the holidays, so tell us the camp section or the nearest beach access point off Point Nepean Road. Waiting near the road with your bags ready helps the driver find you quickly when traffic is heavy.

name: McCrae
description: Taxi and wheelchair taxi in McCrae, day or night. Local rides, hillside pick-ups, Rosebud Hospital and airport transfers. Book online.
intro: Squeezed between the bay and the slopes of Arthurs Seat, McCrae is a narrow strip of homes and holiday houses, and we look after it 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Whether you need a standard taxi to Rosebud or a wheelchair accessible vehicle with a ramp or hoist, Taxi Peninsula can send the right car. Our drivers help door to door, which matters on McCrae’s steeper streets.

The white McCrae Lighthouse stands beside Point Nepean Road, and the historic McCrae Homestead is a reminder that this was one of the earliest settled parts of the peninsula. Above the town, the Arthurs Seat Eagle gondola climbs the escarpment to the summit, so visitors often ask for a lift to or from the base station. Locals mostly travel to Rosebud for shopping and Rosebud Hospital, to Dromana for the cinema and cafes, and further afield to Frankston Hospital, Frankston station or Melbourne Airport via the freeway.

Hillside homes up the side of Arthurs Seat can be tricky to find at night, so a quick note about your driveway or a nearby street helps. For early flights, specialist appointments in the city or a hospital admission, booking ahead gives you peace of mind. Groups can travel together in the Maxi WAT, which carries up to two wheelchairs and six seated passengers, and we take MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts.
local: McCrae is long and thin: Point Nepean Road runs along the water, and the residential streets climb quickly up the lower slopes of Arthurs Seat. Some of those upper streets are steep and winding with limited room to turn, so tell us if your driveway is sharp or your house sits well above the road. The freeway is close by for trips north, which avoids most of the foreshore traffic. In January and on sunny weekends the bay road through McCrae can crawl with beach traffic and Eagle visitors, so allow a little extra time and book ahead if you have a train, flight or appointment to make.

faq.q: Can a taxi get up the steep streets above Point Nepean Road?
faq.a: Yes, our cars regularly handle McCrae’s hillside streets. Where a driveway is very steep or narrow, the driver may stop on the street and help you down to the car instead. If you use a wheelchair, mention the slope when booking so we can plan where the vehicle should park for a safe, level loading spot.

faq.q: Can you take us to the Arthurs Seat Eagle and pick us up later?
faq.a: We can drop you near the Eagle and collect you afterwards, either at the bottom or from the summit car park if you only ride one way. Book the return as “pick up when ready” and let us know which end you’ll finish at, then tap “I’m ready” or call when you’re back on the ground.

faq.q: How do I get from McCrae to Frankston station for a train?
faq.a: We’ll take you directly from your door to Frankston station, usually via the freeway. For an early train into the city, book the night before and add a note about luggage. Many McCrae residents also use us for the reverse trip, booking a pick-up at Frankston when they come home late in the evening.

name: Tootgarook
description: Tootgarook taxi and wheelchair taxi, available 24/7. Trips to Rye, Rosebud Hospital, Frankston and Melbourne Airport. Book online in minutes.
intro: Ask a Tootgarook local where they’re going and the answer is usually Rosebud, Rye or Frankston, and Taxi Peninsula can get you to all three at any time of day. We run sedans for everyday trips and wheelchair accessible vehicles for passengers who travel in their chair, including a Maxi WAT with a hydraulic hoist for heavier power chairs. Book online or call, and your confirmation arrives by SMS or email.

Tootgarook is a relaxed, mostly residential suburb on the bay between Capel Sound and Rye. Point Nepean Road runs along the beach side, holiday houses are mixed in with permanent homes, and behind the town lies the Tootgarook Swamp wetland, an important area for local birdlife. People here travel to Rye for groceries and the foreshore, to Rosebud for Rosebud Hospital and medical appointments, and to Frankston for the hospital, Bayside shopping centre and trains. Longer trips to Melbourne Airport or the city are common too.

Because Tootgarook has plenty of short-stay rentals, visitors often call us without knowing the area well, so check the exact street address before booking. If you’re flying out early, set the pick-up the night before. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers or family members can ride along with the passenger at no fuss. Heading home from Frankston Hospital after a day procedure? Choose “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” when the nurses discharge you, and we’ll send a car down the freeway to collect you.
local: Point Nepean Road carries most traffic through Tootgarook, with Truemans Road leading inland towards the freeway and the back beaches. Summer holidays bring heavy beach traffic along the bay road, and the run between Rosebud and Rye can slow right down on hot afternoons. The residential streets behind the foreshore are a grid of similar-looking courts and avenues, and holiday houses don’t always have clear numbers, so give us a description of the house or a nearby corner. Buses run along Point Nepean Road, but they don’t reach many of the back streets, which is where a door-to-door taxi saves a long walk with shopping or luggage.

faq.q: I’m staying in a holiday rental in Tootgarook. What should I tell you when I book?
faq.a: Give us the full street address from your booking confirmation and, if you can, a short description of the house or a nearby cross street. Some rentals sit behind other properties or have numbers that are hard to see at night. A mobile number we can reach on the day also helps the driver find you quickly.

faq.q: Can you take me from Tootgarook to Frankston for an early train?
faq.a: Yes. Book the trip the night before and set the pick-up time with a little spare for the drive along the freeway. We’ll drop you right at Frankston station. If you’re coming back the same day, you can book the return trip at the same time or call us when your train is nearing Frankston.

faq.q: Can my mum, who uses a power chair, travel with the rest of the family?
faq.a: Yes. The Maxi WAT carries up to two wheelchairs and six seated passengers, and its hydraulic hoist suits heavier power chairs. That makes it handy for family outings from Tootgarook to Rye, Sorrento or a lunch in Rosebud. Let us know the size of the group and the type of chair when you book.

name: Blairgowrie
description: Blairgowrie taxi and wheelchair taxi service, 24 hours. Rides to Sorrento, Rye, Rosebud Hospital, the ferry and Melbourne Airport.
intro: Blairgowrie swaps between two personalities: quiet and local for most of the year, then lively and full of holidaymakers over summer. Taxi Peninsula works through both, around the clock. You can book a sedan for a quick run to Sorrento or Rye, or a wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT when someone needs to travel seated in their wheelchair, with a ramp or hoist and four-point restraints.

The village sits between Rye and Sorrento, with the Blairgowrie Yacht Squadron and its marina on the bay side and the wild back beaches of the national park a short drive south. Shops and cafes line Point Nepean Road, and holiday homes fill the tree-lined streets that rise behind them. Residents travel to Sorrento for dining and the Queenscliff ferry, to Rosebud for Rosebud Hospital, and to Frankston Hospital for specialist care. Visitors often book us for Melbourne Airport transfers at the start and end of a stay.

Summer bookings fill quickly, especially on weekend evenings, so if you’re heading out to dinner or catching a flight, reserve your car early. Groups can ask for the Maxi WAT. We accept MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers travel alongside the passenger, so let us know how many people are coming. Returning from Melbourne Airport at the end of a holiday is easier when you add your flight number, because we track the flight and adjust the pick-up time. Drivers will also help with beach gear, bags and walking frames at the door.
local: Point Nepean Road is the only main road through Blairgowrie, linking you to Sorrento in one direction and Rye in the other, which means a single slow patch can hold everything up. Expect queues in January, on long weekends and around ferry times in Sorrento. Many homes are tucked into sloping, tree-covered blocks along winding streets with no footpaths, and house numbers can be hard to see at night, so describe your driveway or the colour of your letterbox when you book. Back beach car parks along the ocean side are spread out, so name the specific beach if you need collecting from one.

faq.q: Can you meet the ferry at Sorrento and bring us to Blairgowrie?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us which crossing you’re on and we’ll be at the Sorrento terminal to take you to your accommodation in Blairgowrie. Ferries can run late in rough weather, so it’s worth calling us when you’re about to arrive. We can also take you the other way, from home to the terminal for a trip across to Queenscliff.

faq.q: Is it worth booking ahead in summer?
faq.a: Yes, very much so. From Christmas through January, and on warm weekends, Blairgowrie and the neighbouring towns are packed and demand for taxis rises sharply. Booking ahead, especially for evening dinners in Sorrento or early airport runs, means a car is set aside for you instead of waiting for one to become free.

faq.q: Can you take me home after a night out in Sorrento or Rye?
faq.a: Of course. Many Blairgowrie residents and visitors book a return trip from a restaurant or the pub in Sorrento or Rye. You can set a fixed time or use “pick up when ready” and let us know when you’re leaving. The driver will drop you at your door rather than at the main road.

name: Safety Beach
description: Taxi and wheelchair taxi in Safety Beach, 24/7. Martha Cove pick-ups, Mornington, Frankston Hospital and Melbourne Airport transfers.
intro: With Martha Cove at one end and Dromana at the other, Safety Beach is a busy little bayside suburb, and Taxi Peninsula serves it 24 hours a day, every day of the year. Book a sedan for errands or nights out, or a wheelchair accessible vehicle with a rear ramp or hydraulic hoist for passengers who stay in their chair. Our drivers help from your door to the car and back again.

The suburb has a long, sheltered beach backed by newer housing estates, the Martha Cove marina with its waterfront restaurants and apartments, and the Safety Beach Country Club golf course. Arthurs Seat rises behind the town, and the Mornington Peninsula Freeway runs close by, so Melbourne Airport and the city are easy trips. Locals often travel to Mornington for shopping and The Bays Hospital, to Frankston Hospital for specialist care, and to Rosebud Hospital for nearer appointments.

If you’re booking an airport run, add your flight number and we’ll track the flight for your return pick-up. Booking ahead is wise for early starts and hospital admissions. Larger family groups or friends travelling with a wheelchair user can use the Maxi WAT, and we take MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts, with carers riding alongside. Hospital trips are just as simple: for a discharge from Frankston Hospital or The Bays, pick “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” once you’re cleared to go home. The driver will see you to your front door.
local: Safety Beach is easy to get in and out of, thanks to the freeway close by and the bay road running through to Dromana and Mount Martha. Traffic builds on summer weekends when beachgoers and boaties head to the foreshore and Martha Cove. Within the estates, many streets curve and loop back on themselves, and some newer houses aren’t well shown on older maps, so a cross street helps. If you’re being collected from Martha Cove, name the restaurant, apartment building or marina area so the driver knows where to wait. Night pick-ups from the foreshore are quickest from a well-lit spot by the road.

faq.q: Can you pick us up after dinner at Martha Cove?
faq.a: Yes. Martha Cove is a common pick-up point for us. When booking, tell us the restaurant or building you’re at so the driver can wait in the right spot. You can set a time or choose “pick up when ready” and let us know once you’ve paid the bill. We’ll take you home anywhere on the peninsula or further.

faq.q: What’s the easiest way to get from Safety Beach to Mornington?
faq.a: A taxi straight along the bay or via the freeway is usually the simplest choice, especially if you’re carrying shopping or heading to The Bays Hospital. We drop at the door of your appointment or at Main Street. If you need to come home at an uncertain time, book the return as “pick up when ready”.

faq.q: We’re flying into Melbourne Airport. Can you meet us and bring us to Safety Beach?
faq.a: Yes. Add your flight number when booking and we’ll track the flight, so if it lands early or late the pick-up time adjusts. The driver will take you straight down to Safety Beach. Let us know about any extra luggage, prams or a wheelchair so we send a vehicle with enough room.

name: Boneo
description: Boneo taxi and wheelchair taxi for rural properties, 24/7. Trips to Rosebud Hospital, Peninsula Hot Springs, Frankston and the airport.
intro: Boneo is open country: paddocks, horse properties, market gardens and homes set well back from the road on the plains south of Rosebud. Taxi Peninsula serves it day and night, sending a sedan for regular trips or a wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT for people who travel in their chair. Our drivers are used to rural pick-ups and will help you from the house to the car.

Boneo Road is the main route through the area, running from Rosebud towards Cape Schanck and the ocean coast, with Browns Road among the roads crossing it. There’s no real town centre, so residents head to Rosebud for groceries, the pharmacy and Rosebud Hospital, and to Frankston for the hospital, larger shops and trains. Peninsula Hot Springs and the golf courses of Fingal and Cape Schanck are close by, so visitors staying in Boneo often book us to get there and back.

Because Boneo addresses can be hard to find, especially after dark, tell us about long driveways, gates and landmarks when you book. Early flights and morning specialist appointments are best arranged the night before. We take MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and a carer or family member is welcome to come along. For hospital visits, our “pick up when ready” option means you don’t have to guess how long a Rosebud Hospital or Frankston Hospital appointment will run. Larger households, or visitors travelling with a wheelchair user, can ride together in the Maxi WAT, whose hydraulic hoist suits heavier power chairs.
local: Out here, distances feel longer than in town, and there are few streetlights once you leave Boneo Road. Many properties sit at the end of long gravel driveways or behind farm gates, and some side roads are unsealed, so please give us clear directions, mention gate codes, and tell us whether the driver should come to the house or wait at the road. Mobile reception can be patchy in some pockets, so a landline or alternative number is useful. Traffic is usually light, but Boneo Road gets busier in summer with people heading to the back beaches and the hot springs. Public transport doesn’t really reach most of Boneo.

faq.q: My house is down a long gravel driveway. Will the taxi come to the door?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. Tell us how long the driveway is, whether there’s a gate and where the car can turn around. If the track is very rough or wet, the driver may suggest meeting at the gate instead. For wheelchair passengers we’ll work out a firm, level spot to load safely.

faq.q: Can you take me from Boneo to Peninsula Hot Springs?
faq.a: Yes, it’s a short trip across to Fingal and one we do often. We’ll drop you at the main entry. After a long soak you may not know when you’ll be ready, so book the return as “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” or call us when you’re heading out.

faq.q: Can you get me to Melbourne Airport for an early flight from Boneo?
faq.a: Yes, we run 24 hours, so very early departures are no problem. Book the night before, add your flight details and include directions to your property. We’ll set a pick-up time that leaves you comfortable time at the airport. On your return, your flight number lets us track your arrival.

name: Fingal
description: Fingal taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Rides to and from Peninsula Hot Springs, Moonah Links, Rosebud and Melbourne Airport. Book online.
intro: Most people asking for a taxi to Fingal are going to the hot springs, and Taxi Peninsula is happy to get them there and home again at any hour. We also look after the people who live in Fingal’s scattered rural homes. Book a sedan for a simple trip, or a wheelchair accessible vehicle with a ramp or hoist and proper four-point restraints for passengers who stay in their chair.

Fingal is a quiet stretch of farmland and bush between Boneo, Rye and the ocean coast of the Mornington Peninsula National Park. Peninsula Hot Springs draws visitors from all over Melbourne, and the Moonah Links golf courses are nearby, so we carry plenty of day-trippers, golfers and weekend guests. For residents, everyday trips run to Rosebud and Rye for shopping and to Rosebud Hospital, while Frankston Hospital and Melbourne Airport are common longer journeys.

Bookings for the hot springs are worth making in advance, especially on weekends and public holidays when the area is busy. Groups of friends can share the Maxi WAT, which takes up to two wheelchairs and six seated passengers. MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts are accepted, and carers travel with the passenger they support. Flying in for a spa weekend? Add your flight number and we’ll track it, so the driver is at Melbourne Airport when you actually land rather than when the timetable said. We’re also happy to take you back to your accommodation in Rye, Rosebud or Sorrento after your session.
local: Fingal has no shopping strip, just country roads such as Boneo Road and Browns Road linking farms, wineries, golf courses and the hot springs. Roads are mostly quiet, but there’s little street lighting and some side roads are unsealed, so night pick-ups from private homes need clear directions and a note about gates or long driveways. The area around the hot springs gets busy on weekends and holidays, with cars coming down from the freeway. There’s no practical public transport to most of Fingal, which is why visitors without a car rely on taxis to get between Rosebud, Rye and the springs.

faq.q: Can you collect us from Peninsula Hot Springs after a late session?
faq.a: Yes, we run 24 hours. Book your return trip as “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” or call us when you’re dressed and heading out. If you already know your finish time, you can set it when booking. We’ll take you back to your accommodation anywhere on the peninsula or home to Melbourne.

faq.q: Can a group of friends get to the hot springs together from Melbourne?
faq.a: Yes. The Maxi WAT can carry up to two wheelchairs and six seated passengers, so it suits friends travelling together, including someone who uses a wheelchair. Tell us your group size and pick-up address when booking, and ask for a fixed quote if you’d like to know the fare before the day.

faq.q: Can you take me and my golf clubs to Moonah Links?
faq.a: Yes. Mention your golf bag when you book so we send a car with the right boot space. We’ll drop you at the clubhouse and can bring you back after your round. Booking the return as “pick up when ready” is handy when you’re not sure how long the nineteenth hole will take.

name: Cape Schanck
description: Taxi and wheelchair taxi in Cape Schanck, 24/7. Resort, golf and lighthouse trips, Two Bays Walking Track pick-ups and airport transfers.
intro: Where the peninsula meets Bass Strait, Cape Schanck combines a small residential community with a golf resort, a historic lighthouse and some of the most dramatic coastline in Victoria. Taxi Peninsula serves it around the clock. Choose a sedan for golf days and airport runs, or a wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT for passengers who need to travel seated in their wheelchair.

The RACV Cape Schanck Resort and The National Golf Club bring a steady flow of golfers and guests, while walkers come for the Cape Schanck Lighthouse, Bushrangers Bay and the southern end of the Two Bays Walking Track from Dromana. Homes are spread through bushy estates near the resort and along the coast. Residents travel inland to Rosebud for shopping and Rosebud Hospital, to Frankston for larger appointments, and up the freeway to Melbourne Airport and the city.

Because Cape Schanck is a fair way from the bay towns, booking ahead is the best way to make sure a car is waiting, especially for early flights or a set finish time after a walk or a round. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers can travel with the passenger at no extra fuss. Resort guests arriving from Melbourne Airport can add a flight number so we track the arrival. Golfers should mention their bags when booking, and walkers finishing at the lighthouse can choose “pick up when ready”, then tap “I’m ready” once they’re back at the car park.
local: Boneo Road and Cape Schanck’s other approach roads cross open farmland before reaching the coast, and the area feels remote at night with little street lighting. Within the residential estates, streets wind through tea-tree and coastal scrub, so give us a house description or nearby corner. Car parks for the lighthouse and Bushrangers Bay are separate, so be clear about where you’ll be waiting after a walk. Mobile coverage can drop out along parts of the coastline, so agree on a pick-up time or call us before you set off. Summer weekends and holidays bring extra traffic, but it’s rarely congested.

faq.q: Can you pick up walkers at the end of the Two Bays Walking Track?
faq.a: Yes. Many walkers finish at Cape Schanck and want a lift back to Dromana or their accommodation. Tell us which car park you’ll be waiting at and roughly when you expect to arrive. Because phone reception can be unreliable on the coast, it’s best to call us before you lose signal or set a firm pick-up time.

faq.q: We’re staying at the resort. Can you bring us from Melbourne Airport?
faq.a: Yes. Add your flight number when booking and we’ll track the flight, adjusting the pick-up if it lands early or late. The driver will take you straight to the resort entrance. We can also book your departure trip at the same time, so both ends of your stay are sorted.

faq.q: Can you take a group of golfers with clubs to The National?
faq.a: Yes. Let us know how many players and golf bags there are, and we’ll suggest the right vehicle. A larger group may suit the Maxi WAT, depending on the bags. We’ll drop you at the clubhouse and can collect you after the round, either at a set time or when you call.

name: Main Ridge
description: Main Ridge taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Cellar door trips, rural property pick-ups, Rosebud and Frankston hospitals and airport runs.
intro: Up on the ridge, among vineyards, orchards and patches of tall forest, Main Ridge is one of the quieter corners of the Mornington Peninsula. Taxi Peninsula covers it 24 hours a day. We’ll send a sedan for lunch at a cellar door or a ride to town, and a wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT when a passenger needs to stay in their wheelchair for the trip.

Main Ridge sits on the high ground behind Rosebud and Dromana, around Mornington–Flinders Road and Main Creek Road, with Arthurs Seat State Park on its edge. Visitors come for cool-climate wineries and restaurants and for pick-your-own fruit at Sunny Ridge Strawberry Farm. Residents, many on small farms or acreage, travel down to Rosebud for shopping and Rosebud Hospital, across to Red Hill village, and to Frankston Hospital or Melbourne Airport for longer trips.

There’s no bus service worth relying on up here, so a taxi is often the only option for people who don’t drive. Book ahead for appointments, early flights or a planned day of winery visits. MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts are accepted, and carers come along with the passenger. Winery visitors should mention how many are in the party and whether anyone uses a wheelchair, because the Maxi WAT takes up to two chairs and six seated passengers. For residents, “pick up when ready” takes the guesswork out of getting home from a Rosebud Hospital or Frankston Hospital appointment.
local: Roads on the ridge are narrow, winding and often lined with trees, with sharp bends and the occasional fog bank in winter. Many homes are at the end of long driveways or down unsealed tracks, so give us clear directions, mention gates and let us know where the car can turn. Kangaroos and other wildlife are common at dawn and dusk. On summer weekends and long weekends, traffic to wineries and the strawberry farm can slow things down on Mornington–Flinders Road. Mobile reception can be patchy in places, so include a backup number and agree on a meeting point for winery pick-ups.

faq.q: Can you take us between cellar doors around Main Ridge and Red Hill?
faq.a: Yes. We can drop you at one winery and pick you up for the next, or take you to lunch and home again. Let us know your plan when you book and ask for a fixed quote if you’d like. Setting pick-up times in advance works best, as phone signal can be unreliable in some vineyards.

faq.q: We have family visiting who use a wheelchair. Can they get to Sunny Ridge?
faq.a: Yes. Our wheelchair accessible vehicles have a rear ramp or hydraulic hoist and four-point restraints, and the driver will help at both ends. Tell us how many people are coming. The Maxi WAT can carry two wheelchairs and six seated passengers, which suits family day trips to the farm.

faq.q: How do you find properties on unsealed roads in Main Ridge?
faq.a: With good directions from you. When booking, mention the road name, any gate or property name, how long the driveway is, and a landmark such as a winery or corner. If it’s your first booking with us, a quick note about where the driver should stop saves time on the day.

name: Merricks
description: Merricks taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Rides to Pt. Leo Estate, local wineries, Frankston Hospital and Melbourne Airport. Book online.
intro: Blink on the Frankston–Flinders Road and you might miss Merricks, a tiny settlement surrounded by vineyards and farmland near Western Port. Taxi Peninsula serves the area around the clock, whether you need a standard taxi for a quick trip or a wheelchair accessible vehicle with a ramp or hoist. Book online in about two minutes and you’ll get a confirmation by SMS or email.

Merricks is known for its food and wine. Pt. Leo Estate, with its sculpture park and restaurants, sits on the coastal side, and small wineries and farm gates are dotted along the back roads towards Red Hill. Residents head to Balnarring for everyday shopping, to Hastings or Mornington for bigger errands, and to Frankston Hospital or Rosebud Hospital for medical care. Melbourne Airport trips run north via the freeway.

Lunch and dinner bookings are a big part of what we do here, so if you’re planning a long afternoon at a winery, arrange your trip home in advance. We take MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers or support workers ride with the passenger. Groups can ask for the Maxi WAT. Residents use us just as often for practical trips: a specialist visit in Frankston, a pharmacy run to Balnarring or a ride home after a day procedure, where “pick up when ready” lets you tap “I’m ready” once you’re discharged. For airport runs, add your flight number so we can track an inbound flight.
local: Frankston–Flinders Road runs straight through Merricks, carrying traffic between Balnarring and Flinders, and it’s a fast country road with few places to pull over. Side roads lead into farms and vineyards, and some are unsealed, so please tell us the property name, any gate and where the driver should stop. There’s little lighting at night. Summer weekends bring extra visitors to the wineries and the nearby beaches at Point Leo and Merricks Beach, so traffic can bunch up around lunch. Public transport is very limited, so most people without a car rely on taxis to reach Merricks.

faq.q: Can you get us home from lunch at Pt. Leo Estate?
faq.a: Yes. Many people book a taxi to and from the estate so nobody has to drive. Tell us your booking time and where you’re heading afterwards. Choose “pick up when ready” for the return and tap “I’m ready” or call when you’ve finished. We’ll meet you at the main arrival area.

faq.q: Which hospitals do people from Merricks usually travel to?
faq.a: Most public hospital care for the area is at Frankston Hospital or Rosebud Hospital, both run by Peninsula Health. Some people also visit private hospitals in Mornington and Frankston. We’ll drop you at the main entrance; tell us your department or ward when you book. For emergencies, always call 000.

faq.q: Is there a train near Merricks?
faq.a: There’s no station in Merricks. The nearest trains are on the Stony Point line, which runs through Bittern and Crib Point to Frankston. We can take you to one of those stations, or simply drive you all the way to Frankston station for more frequent trains into Melbourne.

name: Merricks North
description: Taxi and wheelchair taxi in Merricks North, 24/7. Farm and acreage pick-ups, Mornington, Frankston Hospital and Melbourne Airport trips.
intro: Merricks North is farm and vineyard country, rolling hills between Red Hill, Balnarring and Moorooduc where houses sit on acreage rather than suburban blocks. Taxi Peninsula serves residents and visitors here 24 hours a day. A sedan suits most trips, while our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT have a ramp or hydraulic hoist for passengers who stay seated in their chair.

The area is largely rural, with cattle, horses, hobby farms and small vineyards spread along winding back roads. There are no shops to speak of, so residents travel to Balnarring for groceries, to Mornington for Main Street, The Bays Hospital and appointments, and to Red Hill for the village and market days. For hospital care, Frankston Hospital is the main destination, and Melbourne Airport trips head north via Peninsula Link.

Out here, a little planning goes a long way. Book early for flights, surgery or specialist visits, and give us clear directions to your property the first time you travel with us. MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts are accepted, and carers or family members can travel with the passenger. After a stay at Frankston Hospital or The Bays, the “pick up when ready” option lets you tap “I’m ready” or call when you’re discharged, so nobody waits around. Coming home from overseas? Add your flight number and we’ll track it. The Maxi WAT can carry a group, or two wheelchair users together.
local: Merricks North is criss-crossed by narrow country roads, some sealed and some gravel, linking it with Balnarring, Bittern, Red Hill and Moorooduc. Properties are often at the end of long driveways, with gates, cattle grids or shared tracks, so let us know exactly where to go and where to turn around. Street numbers on rural roads can be far apart and hard to see in the dark. Traffic is usually light, but summer weekends bring winery visitors and tourists cutting through on their way to Red Hill. With no regular public transport, most people without a car depend on taxis or family for lifts.

faq.q: Our road is unsealed. Can you still pick us up?
faq.a: Yes, we pick up from gravel roads across the peninsula. Tell us the road name, property number and any landmarks, and mention if the surface is rough, steep or boggy after rain. If the driveway isn’t suitable for the car, we can agree on a nearby meeting point instead.

faq.q: Can you take me to The Bays Hospital in Mornington?
faq.a: Yes. We’ll drop you at the main entrance and help you inside if needed. If you don’t know when you’ll be discharged or finished, book the return as “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” or call us when you’re done, and a car will be sent.

faq.q: Can visitors staying on a farm stay in Merricks North get around without a car?
faq.a: Yes. Visitors often book us for trips to Red Hill, wineries, the beaches at Balnarring or Point Leo, and back to Melbourne Airport. Make sure you have the farm’s full address and any gate details, and book return trips in advance, especially on summer weekends.

name: Red Hill
description: Red Hill taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Winery and market day trips, wedding guests, Rosebud and Frankston hospitals and airport runs.
intro: Red Hill is the heart of the peninsula’s wine country, a hilltop village surrounded by cellar doors, restaurants, orchards and acreage. Taxi Peninsula serves locals and visitors here around the clock. Book a sedan for a lunch reservation or a trip to town, or a wheelchair accessible vehicle with a ramp or hoist and four-point restraints for passengers who travel in their chair.

The village has a small cluster of shops and cafes, and the Red Hill Recreation Reserve hosts the Red Hill Market and the annual agricultural show. Main roads such as Arthurs Seat Road, Red Hill Road and Shoreham Road wind over the ridge, linking dozens of wineries including Polperro and many smaller cellar doors. Residents travel down to Dromana and Rosebud for shopping and Rosebud Hospital, to Mornington or Frankston for larger appointments, and further afield to Melbourne Airport or the city.

Weekend and wedding bookings fill quickly, so plan your transport early, especially for evening returns. The Maxi WAT carries groups of friends with up to two wheelchair users. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers ride with the passenger. If you’re travelling down from Melbourne for a long lunch, ask for a fixed quote when you book. Locals heading to Rosebud Hospital or Frankston Hospital can choose “pick up when ready” for the trip home, then tap “I’m ready” or call when finished, and a car will come back up the hill for them.
local: Red Hill’s roads twist over the ridge with steep pinches, sharp bends and narrow verges, and fog can roll in on winter mornings. Many homes and venues sit down long driveways or on unsealed roads, so give us the property name, any gate code and a landmark. On market days, the roads around the recreation reserve get congested, and on summer weekends cellar door traffic can slow travel between Red Hill and the coast. Public transport is minimal on the ridge, which is why many visitors book a taxi to get between venues rather than drive after a tasting.

faq.q: Can you take us to Red Hill Market and back?
faq.a: Yes. Market days are busy, so book ahead and let us know if you’ll have bags or bulky purchases. We’ll drop you as close to the reserve as traffic allows and can collect you at a set time or when you call. Agree on a meeting point near the entrance, as the car park can be crowded.

faq.q: Can you drive us between wineries so nobody has to drive?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us which cellar doors you plan to visit and roughly when, and we’ll organise drop-offs and pick-ups. You can ask for a fixed quote ahead of time. Booking specific times for each leg is easiest, since mobile reception can drop in and out among the vineyards.

faq.q: We have guests travelling to a Red Hill wedding. Can you help?
faq.a: Yes. We can bring guests from their accommodation to the venue and take them home at the end of the night. Book early and give us the venue name, guest numbers and finishing time. Guests who use a wheelchair can travel in an accessible vehicle with their partner or carer.

name: Red Hill South
description: Taxi and wheelchair taxi in Red Hill South, 24/7. Trips to Montalto, Port Phillip Estate, wedding venues, hospitals and the airport.
intro: Cellar doors, restaurants and wedding venues line the roads of Red Hill South, the slope that drops from the Red Hill ridge towards Shoreham and Western Port. Taxi Peninsula serves the area day and night. A sedan covers most trips, and our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT can take passengers who stay seated in their chair, with a ramp or hydraulic hoist and four-point restraints.

Some of the peninsula’s best-known wineries are here, including Montalto with its sculpture trail, Port Phillip Estate and Paringa Estate, along with smaller family-run cellar doors and farm gates. Shoreham Road and Red Hill Road carry most of the traffic. Local residents head up to Red Hill village for the store and market, down to Dromana or Rosebud for shopping and Rosebud Hospital, and to Frankston Hospital for specialist care. Airport trips go north via the freeway.

For long lunches, celebrations and weddings, book your return trip in advance so you’re not left waiting at the end of the day. Groups can share the Maxi WAT. MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts are welcome, and carers travel with the passenger. Guests flying in for a wedding can add their flight number, and we’ll track it for the airport pick-up. Ask for a fixed quote for trips from Melbourne. Residents going to Frankston Hospital or Rosebud Hospital can use “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” when done, rather than sitting in a waiting room.
local: Red Hill South is a mix of vineyard estates, acreage and bush blocks on hilly, winding roads. Several venues have long private driveways, and some homes are on unsealed roads with gates and limited turning space, so give us clear directions and the property name. Night pick-ups are dark, with few streetlights, so wait somewhere visible near the main entrance. Summer weekends, public holidays and wedding season bring plenty of visitors, and Shoreham Road can get busy around lunchtime. There’s no regular bus service through most of Red Hill South, so taxis fill the gap for anyone not driving.

faq.q: Can you pick us up after a wedding reception in Red Hill South?
faq.a: Yes. Let us know the venue, finishing time and how many guests need a ride, and book well before the day. We’ll have a car waiting at the venue’s main entrance. If plans change on the night, call us. Guests who use a wheelchair can travel with a partner or carer in an accessible vehicle.

faq.q: Can you drive us from Melbourne for lunch at Montalto and back again?
faq.a: Yes. We’ll pick you up anywhere in Melbourne, take you to the restaurant and bring you home afterwards. Ask for a fixed quote when booking if you’d like to know the fare ahead of time. Using “pick up when ready” for the return means you won’t have to rush dessert.

faq.q: Do you know the wineries and venues around Red Hill South?
faq.a: Our drivers travel these roads regularly and know the main estates and venues. For smaller cellar doors or private properties, include the full address and any gate details when booking. Telling us where you’ll be waiting, such as the cellar door or restaurant entrance, helps us find you quickly.

name: Crib Point
description: Crib Point taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Trips to Stony Point ferries, Frankston Hospital and station, HMAS Cerberus and the airport.
intro: Crib Point sits on the shore of Western Port, next door to the HMAS Cerberus navy base and a short drive from the Stony Point ferry. Taxi Peninsula covers the town day and night with sedans for everyday trips and wheelchair accessible vehicles for people who need to travel in their chair. Bookings take about two minutes online, with confirmation by SMS or email.

It’s a relaxed, mostly residential town with a small shopping strip, foreshore reserves and a station on the Stony Point line. Navy families, retirees and longtime locals all live here. Common trips include Hastings for supermarkets and services, Frankston for the hospital, Bayside Shopping Centre and metro trains, and Stony Point for ferries to French Island and Phillip Island. Mornington, Rosebud Hospital and Melbourne Airport are also regular destinations.

If you’re catching an early flight, a ferry or a train connection, book ahead so your car is lined up. Groups and families can ask for the Maxi WAT. We accept MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts, and a carer or support worker can travel with the passenger. For Frankston Hospital trips, especially discharges, choose “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” or call when the ward lets you go. Returning to Crib Point after a holiday? Add your flight number when booking from Melbourne Airport and we’ll track your arrival. Drivers help with bags and walking aids at both ends.
local: Frankston–Flinders Road runs past Crib Point, with the town spreading towards the water along quiet residential streets. Just to the south, Stony Point marks the ferry terminal and the end of the train line. Trains on the Stony Point line run less often than metro services, so a taxi to Frankston is often quicker when timing matters. Traffic is usually light, though summer brings extra visitors heading for the ferries. Some streets near the foreshore are narrow or unsealed, so give us a cross street when booking. Ferry passengers with luggage are best collected right at the terminal rather than out on the main road.

faq.q: Can you meet the ferry at Stony Point and take us home to Crib Point?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us which ferry you’re on and we’ll be waiting at Stony Point. Ferries can be delayed by weather, so call us once you’re about to dock if times change. We can also take you from home to the terminal for an outgoing crossing to French Island or Phillip Island.

faq.q: Is it quicker to take a taxi to Frankston than the train?
faq.a: Often, yes, especially if you’d otherwise wait for a Stony Point line connection. A taxi goes straight from your door to Frankston station, Frankston Hospital or Bayside Shopping Centre. If you’re travelling with luggage, a wheelchair or young children, door-to-door transport also saves you a change of train.

faq.q: Do you take people to and from HMAS Cerberus?
faq.a: Yes, we carry navy personnel, visitors and family members to and from the base area. Access to the base itself is managed by Defence, so make sure you have the right arrangements in place and tell us when booking where you need to be dropped. We’ll take you to the entry point.

name: Shoreham
description: Shoreham taxi and wheelchair taxi service, 24/7. Beach and camping pick-ups, Red Hill wineries, Frankston Hospital and airport trips.
intro: Shoreham is small, leafy and quiet for most of the year, a Western Port beach village tucked below the Red Hill ridge. Taxi Peninsula serves it 24 hours a day. You can book a sedan for a ride up to the wineries or into town, or a wheelchair accessible vehicle with a ramp or hoist and four-point restraints when a passenger needs to stay in their wheelchair.

The village centres on its foreshore, with a sheltered beach, a camping ground among the trees and views across Western Port to Phillip Island. Shoreham Road climbs inland to Red Hill South and Red Hill, where cellar doors such as Montalto and Port Phillip Estate are only a short drive away. Locals shop in Balnarring or Red Hill, and travel further to Rosebud Hospital, Frankston Hospital, Mornington or Melbourne Airport.

In summer, the camping ground and holiday homes fill up, so booking ahead is a good idea for dinners out and airport trips. Larger groups can use the Maxi WAT. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers can ride alongside the passenger. Residents heading to a specialist or day surgery at Frankston Hospital or Rosebud Hospital can use “pick up when ready”, then tap “I’m ready” or call when they’re finished. For Melbourne Airport trips, add your flight number so we can track your return. Weekend visitors can ask for a fixed quote from Melbourne.
local: Shoreham is reached via Frankston–Flinders Road or Shoreham Road from Red Hill, both winding country routes with little lighting at night. Inside the village, streets are narrow and leafy, and some homes are set back on bush blocks or along unsealed roads, so let us know where the driver should stop. Over the summer holidays the foreshore camping ground and beach car parks are busy, and traffic builds on Frankston–Flinders Road on weekends. There’s very limited public transport, so taxis are often the easiest way for visitors and residents without a car to reach Balnarring, Red Hill or the hospitals.

faq.q: Can you collect us from the Shoreham foreshore camping ground?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us your site or the nearest landmark, and the driver will meet you there or at the camp entrance. In peak season the area is busy, so having your bags packed and waiting near the road speeds things up. We can take you anywhere on the peninsula or back to Melbourne.

faq.q: Can you take us up to Red Hill for dinner and bring us back?
faq.a: Yes. It’s a short drive up Shoreham Road to many of the Red Hill restaurants and cellar doors. Book your outward trip with a set time and use “pick up when ready” for the return. On summer weekends, book a day or two ahead to make sure a car is available.

faq.q: Is there a bus from Shoreham to the hospital?
faq.a: Public transport from Shoreham is very limited, so most people without a car use a taxi for hospital trips. We’ll take you door to door to Frankston Hospital or Rosebud Hospital and drop you at the main entrance. For appointments with an uncertain finish time, book the return as “pick up when ready”.

name: Somers
description: Somers taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Rides to Balnarring, Hastings, Frankston Hospital, Coolart Wetlands and Melbourne Airport.
intro: Somers is a tight-knit beach village on Western Port, with sandy streets, coastal bush and a long, quiet beach. Taxi Peninsula serves it around the clock. Book a sedan for a trip to the shops or the station, or a wheelchair accessible vehicle when someone needs to travel seated in their wheelchair, with a ramp or hoist and four-point restraints.

The village is home to the Somers Yacht Club, the general store and Lord Somers Camp, while Coolart Wetlands and Homestead sits on the edge of town with its birdlife and historic house. Many residents commute or travel for shopping and services to Balnarring, Hastings or Frankston. Frankston Hospital is the main public hospital for the area, and trips to Melbourne Airport, the city or Mornington are common. Families staying in holiday houses over summer often book us for trips into town, dinners in Balnarring or Red Hill, and the ride back to the city at the end of the week.

Somers has very little public transport, so it pays to book ahead for appointments, early flights or train connections. Groups and families can ask for the Maxi WAT. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers travel with the passenger. For hospital visits, “pick up when ready” lets you tap “I’m ready” or call once you’re finished at Frankston Hospital, and for flights home, adding your flight number lets us track it.
local: Somers is reached from Frankston–Flinders Road via Lord Somers Road and nearby roads, and the village itself is quiet with low traffic most of the year. Many streets are narrow, some are unsealed, and homes sit among tea-tree and banksia on bush blocks, so give us a house description, colour or landmark. There are few streetlights, and house numbers can be hard to spot at night. In summer, holidaymakers and school camp groups add to local traffic. The nearest train stations are on the Stony Point line, and buses are limited, so taxis are often the practical choice.

faq.q: Can you take a group to Lord Somers Camp?
faq.a: Yes. Let us know the group size, pick-up point and any luggage or equipment when you book. The Maxi WAT can carry up to two wheelchairs and six seated passengers, which suits small groups. For larger parties, tell us your numbers and we’ll talk through what’s needed for the trip.

faq.q: Can you take me to the train at Bittern or Frankston?
faq.a: Yes. We can drop you at a nearby Stony Point line station or take you all the way to Frankston station for more frequent trains. If you’re catching an early service, book the night before. We can also meet you at the station when you return, so you’re not left waiting for a bus.

faq.q: Can you take us to Coolart Wetlands and Homestead?
faq.a: Yes. It’s a short trip from most of Somers, and we can drop you at the car park near the entrance. If you’re not sure how long you’ll spend watching the birds or exploring the gardens, book the return as “pick up when ready” and call us when you’re finished.

name: Balnarring
description: Balnarring taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Local shopping trips, Bittern station, Frankston Hospital, Mornington and Melbourne Airport.
intro: For the eastern side of the peninsula, Balnarring is the everyday hub, with a supermarket, chemist, cafes and medical services serving nearby Somers, Merricks and Bittern. Taxi Peninsula serves the town and surrounding farms 24 hours a day. A sedan suits most trips, while our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT carry passengers who stay in their wheelchair, with drivers helping door to door.

The village shopping centre sits just off Frankston–Flinders Road, and Balnarring Beach, with its foreshore and camping ground, is a short drive towards Western Port. Around the town, lifestyle blocks and vineyards spread across the hills toward Merricks North and Red Hill. Residents travel to Hastings and Mornington for larger shopping, to Frankston Hospital for specialist and emergency care, and to the Stony Point line stations for trains. Melbourne Airport trips run via Peninsula Link.

If you have an appointment or flight to catch, book ahead to secure your car. We take MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers can travel with the passenger. Families or groups can ask for the Maxi WAT. For discharges and day procedures at Frankston Hospital or The Bays, “pick up when ready” means you tap “I’m ready” or call when you’re cleared, and we send a car. Flying home? Add your flight number when booking from Melbourne Airport so we can track your arrival. Ask for a fixed quote for longer trips.
local: Frankston–Flinders Road is the main road through Balnarring, Balnarring Road heads north-west towards Moorooduc, and local roads run down to Balnarring Beach and Somers. Traffic is generally light, but summer weekends bring beachgoers and winery visitors through town. Outside the village, many properties are on acreage with long driveways and some unsealed roads, so tell us about gates and where the driver can turn. At Balnarring Beach, the foreshore can be busy in peak season, so name the car park or camp entrance. Buses are infrequent, and the nearest trains are at Bittern on the Stony Point line.

faq.q: Can you take me to Bittern station for a train?
faq.a: Yes. Bittern station on the Stony Point line is a short trip from Balnarring. If you’re heading into Melbourne, we can also take you straight to Frankston station for more frequent metro trains, which saves a change. Book early services the night before and let us know about luggage.

faq.q: Can you help me with a shopping trip to Hastings or Mornington?
faq.a: Yes. Our drivers help door to door, including with shopping bags. We can drop you at the shopping centre or main street and pick you up at a set time, or you can use “pick up when ready” and call when you’ve finished. MPTP cards are accepted for eligible passengers.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from the Balnarring Beach camping ground?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us your site number or the nearest landmark, and the driver will meet you at the camp entrance or a spot you agree on. During school holidays, the foreshore is busy, so it helps to be waiting with bags ready. We can take you home to Melbourne or to Melbourne Airport.

name: St Andrews Beach
description: St Andrews Beach taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Pick-ups on sandy back roads, trips to Rye, Rosebud Hospital and Melbourne Airport.
intro: Sandy tracks, tea-tree scrub and the roar of the surf define St Andrews Beach, a quiet settlement on the ocean side of the peninsula behind Rye. Taxi Peninsula serves it day and night. We send a sedan for everyday trips, or a wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT with a ramp or hydraulic hoist for passengers who need to stay in their wheelchair.

Homes and holiday houses here are spread through coastal bush between the Mornington Peninsula National Park and the farmland of Fingal. The back beach is popular with surfers and walkers, though it’s known for strong currents. There are no shops, so residents head to Rye for groceries and the foreshore, to Rosebud for Rosebud Hospital and appointments, and to Frankston for the hospital and trains. Visitors staying in rentals often book us for Melbourne Airport transfers.

Many addresses can be confusing on a first visit, so give us clear directions when booking. Early flights and appointments are best organised the night before. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers or family can travel with the passenger. Holidaymakers arriving at Melbourne Airport can add a flight number so we track the arrival time. Residents using us for Rosebud Hospital or Frankston Hospital appointments can pick “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” or call when finished. Groups and wheelchair users can ask for the Maxi WAT, which takes two chairs and six seated passengers.
local: St Andrews Beach is a network of sandy, mostly unsealed roads off the main routes to Rye and Fingal, and some streets are narrow, rutted or soft after heavy rain. Please describe your driveway, any gate and whether a car can turn around, and tell us if the driver should meet you at the road. There’s no street lighting on most roads, and house numbers can be hard to see at night. Summer weekends bring surfers and beachgoers, and the beach car park fills on warm days. There’s no regular public transport here, so taxis are a practical way to reach Rye or Rosebud.

faq.q: The roads near my house are sandy and unsealed. Can a taxi get in?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Tell us how the road is after rain, whether your driveway is soft, and if there’s a gate. If a section isn’t suitable for the vehicle, the driver will arrange to meet you at the nearest firm spot. For wheelchair passengers, a level, firm loading area is important.

faq.q: Can you pick me up from the beach car park after a surf or walk?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us which car park you’ll be at and when you expect to finish. On busy days the car park can fill up, so wait somewhere visible near the entrance. If your timing is uncertain, book as “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” or call us when you’re back.

faq.q: How do I get from St Andrews Beach to Rye or Rosebud for shopping?
faq.a: A taxi is the simplest way, as there’s no regular bus service from St Andrews Beach. We’ll take you to the supermarket or shops in Rye or Rosebud, and our drivers can help with bags on the way home. You can set a return time or call us when you’re ready.

name: Arthurs Seat
description: Arthurs Seat taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Rides to the Eagle gondola, summit, gardens and homes on the mountain, plus airport trips.
intro: Arthurs Seat is both a mountain and a place people live, and Taxi Peninsula serves residents and visitors around the clock. We send sedans for everyday trips and wheelchair accessible vehicles with a ramp or hydraulic hoist for passengers who stay seated in their wheelchair. Bookings take about two minutes online, and you’ll get confirmation by SMS or email.

Rising above Dromana, McCrae and Rosebud, Arthurs Seat offers wide views over Port Phillip. Visitors come for Arthurs Seat State Park, the summit lookouts, Seawinds Gardens and the Arthurs Seat Eagle gondola, which runs between the base and the summit. Enchanted Adventure Garden is popular with families. Residents live along winding roads in bushland and on acreage, and travel down to Dromana and Rosebud for shopping and Rosebud Hospital, and to Frankston Hospital or Melbourne Airport for longer trips.

Weekends and holidays are busy on the mountain, so book ahead if you’re visiting or need a ride for an appointment. Groups can share the Maxi WAT. MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts are accepted, and carers travel with the passenger. Families with a grandparent in a power chair can travel together in the Maxi WAT, which has a hydraulic hoist and room for six seated passengers. Residents heading to Rosebud Hospital or Frankston Hospital can choose “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” when finished, and a car will come back up the mountain. For flights, add your flight number.
local: Arthurs Seat Road climbs the escarpment with tight bends and steep grades, and other roads around the summit are narrow and wooded. Fog and low cloud can settle on the mountain, especially in winter. Many homes are tucked down long driveways or along bush tracks, some unsealed, so give us directions and tell us where the driver can turn. Weekends, school holidays and fine days bring heavy visitor traffic to the summit and the Eagle. If you’re being collected from a park or garden, name the car park or entrance, as several attractions share the same roads.

faq.q: Can you take us to the top so we can ride the Eagle down?
faq.a: Yes. We can drop you at the summit and meet you at the bottom, or the other way round. Tell us which end you’re starting from, and book your second trip as “pick up when ready”. Tap “I’m ready” or call us once you’re off the gondola, and a car will be sent.

faq.q: Can a wheelchair user visit the summit lookouts?
faq.a: We can take wheelchair users to the summit car park in an accessible vehicle with four-point restraints. Accessibility of individual paths, gardens and the gondola is managed by those attractions, so check with them before you go. Our driver will help you from the vehicle to the entrance or lookout area.

faq.q: Do you pick up from homes on the mountain roads?
faq.a: Yes, we pick up from homes all over Arthurs Seat. Some driveways are steep, narrow or unsealed, so tell us about gates, slopes and turning space when booking. If the driveway isn’t suitable, we can agree on a meeting point at the road for a safe pick-up.

name: HMAS Cerberus
description: Taxi and wheelchair taxi for HMAS Cerberus, 24/7. Trips for navy members, visitors and families to Frankston, the airport and Melbourne.
intro: HMAS Cerberus is the Royal Australian Navy’s training base on Western Port, next to Crib Point, and Taxi Peninsula provides taxis for navy members, visitors and families around the clock. We run sedans for trips to the station, shops or airport, and wheelchair accessible vehicles for passengers who travel in their chair, including grandparents or relatives coming to a special occasion.

The base is surrounded by bush and farmland, with Crib Point, Hastings and Balnarring nearby. Navy members often travel to Frankston for trains and shopping, to Melbourne Airport for leave and postings, and into the city on weekends. Visiting family and friends usually stay in nearby towns or along the peninsula, and need transport to and from the base area on important days. Frankston Hospital and The Bays Hospital in Mornington are the main hospitals in the region.

Book ahead for flights, weekend leave and special events, when demand rises. Families can travel together in the Maxi WAT, which carries up to two wheelchairs and six seated passengers. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers can ride with the passenger. Arriving at Melbourne Airport? Add your flight number and we’ll track it, so a delay doesn’t leave anyone stranded. For appointments at Frankston Hospital, choose “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” or call when finished. Ask for a fixed quote if you’d like the fare confirmed before travel.
local: The base is reached via Frankston–Flinders Road, with Crib Point and Stony Point to one side and Hastings to the north. Base access is controlled by Defence, so you’ll need the right arrangements to enter, and we’ll drop you at the entry point you’re directed to. Traffic can be heavier on days with large events at the base. The Stony Point train line passes nearby, but services are less frequent than metro trains, so many people take a taxi to Frankston station. For pick-ups, tell us the gate or meeting point and a contact number.

faq.q: Can the taxi drive onto the base?
faq.a: Base access is controlled by Defence, so we can’t promise entry. We’ll take you to the gate or meeting point you’ve been directed to, and drop you there. If you’re a visitor, make sure your access is arranged in advance. When booking, tell us where you need to go and give us a contact number.

faq.q: We’re family coming for a special event at the base. Can you help?
faq.a: Yes. We can collect you from Melbourne Airport, Frankston station or your accommodation and bring you to the base area. Book early, as these days can be busy. If a relative uses a wheelchair, our accessible vehicles have ramps or hoists and four-point restraints, and the family can travel together.

faq.q: Can you take me to Melbourne Airport for leave?
faq.a: Yes, we run 24 hours. Book ahead, add your flight details and tell us your pick-up point. If you’re coming back to the base, give us your arrival flight number and we’ll track it. Groups of members going on leave together can share a car or the Maxi WAT.

name: Flinders
description: Flinders taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Rides to the golf club, pier, Red Hill wineries, Rosebud and Frankston hospitals and airport.
intro: At the southern tip of the peninsula, where Western Port opens to Bass Strait, Flinders is a historic seaside village with a pier, a clifftop golf course and a strong local community. Taxi Peninsula serves it 24 hours a day. A sedan handles most trips, and our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT carry passengers who stay seated in their chair, with drivers helping door to door.

Cook Street is the heart of town, with cafes and local shops. Flinders Pier, Mushroom Reef Marine Sanctuary and the ocean coast to West Head draw walkers, divers and families, and Flinders Golf Club is set high above the water. Residents travel up to Red Hill and Main Ridge, to Rosebud for shopping and Rosebud Hospital, and to Frankston Hospital for specialist care. Melbourne Airport trips head north through the peninsula.

Because Flinders is at the end of the road, booking ahead is wise for flights, appointments and dinners out. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers can travel with the passenger. Groups can share the Maxi WAT. For Frankston Hospital or Rosebud Hospital appointments, “pick up when ready” lets you tap “I’m ready” or call when you’re finished, so you aren’t left waiting. Coming home from Melbourne Airport? Add your flight number when booking and we’ll track it. Holiday visitors can ask for a fixed quote from Melbourne before they travel.
local: Flinders sits where Frankston–Flinders Road and Mornington–Flinders Road meet, both winding country roads with sharp bends and few overtaking spots. The town feels a long way from the bay side, so allow a little extra time for pick-ups. Summer weekends and holidays bring visitors to the pier, golf club and beaches, and parking near Cook Street can be tight. Homes on the edge of town are often set on acreage or bush blocks with long driveways, so give us clear directions. Buses are infrequent, so many residents and visitors use taxis.

faq.q: Can you take me from Flinders to Frankston Hospital?
faq.a: Yes. We’ll take you door to door and drop you at the main entrance; tell us your department or ward when you book. For appointments or discharges with uncertain timing, use “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” or call us when you’re finished. For emergencies, always call 000.

faq.q: Can you get me and my clubs to Flinders Golf Club?
faq.a: Yes. Mention your golf bag when booking so we send a car with enough boot space. We’ll drop you at the clubhouse and can pick you up after your round at a set time or when you call. Groups of golfers can ask about larger vehicles.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead in summer?
faq.a: It’s a good idea. Flinders is at the far end of the peninsula, and summer weekends and holidays are busy. Booking ahead means a car is set aside for you, particularly for early flights, evening dinners or trips home from Red Hill or Rosebud.

name: Point Leo
description: Point Leo taxi and wheelchair taxi, 24/7. Surf beach and camping pick-ups, Pt. Leo Estate, Red Hill, hospitals and Melbourne Airport.
intro: Point Leo is a surf beach first and a settlement second, a small cluster of holiday homes and a big foreshore camping ground on the Western Port coast. Taxi Peninsula serves it day and night. We send sedans for quick trips and wheelchair accessible vehicles with a ramp or hydraulic hoist and four-point restraints for passengers who travel in their wheelchair.

The beach is one of the peninsula’s best-known surf spots, popular with learners and experienced surfers alike, and the foreshore camping ground fills up every summer. Just inland, Pt. Leo Estate and its sculpture park draw diners and art lovers, and Point Leo Road climbs towards Red Hill and its wineries. For shopping and services, people head to Balnarring, Red Hill or Rosebud, and further to Frankston Hospital or Melbourne Airport. Surfers and campers often arrive without a car and rely on us to get to the beach and back.

Summer and long weekends are the busiest times, so book ahead for airport transfers, dinners or trips home. Groups can share the Maxi WAT. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers can ride with the passenger. Campers flying home can add their flight number for return pick-ups, and we’ll track it. Locals heading to Frankston Hospital or Rosebud Hospital can choose “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” or call when finished. Ask for a fixed quote for trips from Melbourne.
local: Point Leo is reached from Frankston–Flinders Road or via Point Leo Road from Red Hill. Roads near the beach are narrow, and the foreshore car parks and camping ground get crowded on summer days. There’s little street lighting, so night pick-ups are easier from a clear, visible spot near the entrance to the camping ground or a car park. Holiday homes are tucked among trees, sometimes with unclear numbers, so describe your house or give us a landmark. There’s no regular public transport, so taxis are often the easiest way for visitors to get around without a car.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from the Point Leo camping ground?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us your site number or a landmark, and the driver will meet you at the camp entrance or a spot you agree on. During summer, the camping ground is busy, so waiting near the road with your bags ready helps. We can take you home or to Melbourne Airport.

faq.q: Can you take us to Pt. Leo Estate for lunch?
faq.a: Yes. It’s a short trip from the beach and holiday homes, and we can take you there from anywhere on the peninsula or Melbourne. Use “pick up when ready” for the return, and tap “I’m ready” or call us when you’re finished, so nobody needs to drive.

faq.q: Is there public transport to Point Leo?
faq.a: Public transport to Point Leo is very limited, so most visitors without a car use taxis. We can collect you from Frankston station or Melbourne Airport and bring you down to the beach or your accommodation. Book ahead for summer weekends, when demand is high.

name: Bittern
description: Taxi and wheelchair accessible taxi service in Bittern, open 24/7 for station runs, hospital visits, airport trips and local errands.
intro: Bittern sits between Hastings and Balnarring on the Western Port side of the Peninsula, and Taxi Peninsula covers it around the clock. We run standard sedans for everyday trips and wheelchair accessible vehicles for passengers who travel seated in their chair, so a household can use one service whether Mum needs the ramp van or the teenagers just need a lift home from Frankston late at night.

Life in Bittern runs along Frankston-Flinders Road, with quiet residential streets spreading towards the water and the bushland edges of town. Bittern station is on the Stony Point line, which is handy but not frequent, so many locals take a taxi to Frankston station to connect with the metropolitan Frankston line. Other regular trips take people to Frankston Hospital, the shops and services in Hastings, Rosebud Hospital on the bay side, and further afield to Melbourne Airport. Residents with family at HMAS Cerberus in nearby Crib Point also use us for visits and drop-offs.

If you have an early flight or a specialist appointment in Frankston or the city, book the evening before so a car is allocated for you. Our Maxi WAT carries two wheelchairs and up to six seated passengers, which suits family outings or a small group heading to a function. We accept MPTP cards, and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and a carer rides with the passenger. Drivers help from your front door to the vehicle and back again.
local: Frankston-Flinders Road is the main spine through Bittern and links north to Somerville and Baxter and south to Balnarring. The Stony Point line stops at Bittern, but services are less frequent than on the metropolitan network, so allow for connections at Frankston. Many streets off the main road are unsealed or narrow, and some rural-style properties have long driveways or gates; let us know when booking if the driver should come right up to the house or wait at the road. Summer weekends bring more traffic towards the Western Port beaches. Late-night trips home from Frankston or Hastings are a regular booking too, so mention if you will be waiting outside a venue.

faq.q: Can you take me from Bittern to Frankston station to catch a train to the city?
faq.a: Yes. Plenty of Bittern residents prefer a taxi to Frankston station over waiting for a Stony Point line connection. We drop you at the station forecourt so you can walk straight to the platforms. Booking ahead is wise for early weekday trains, and if you travel in a wheelchair our ramp van can take you there and you can continue on the metropolitan network.

faq.q: My property in Bittern is on a gravel road. Will the driver find it?
faq.a: Our drivers are used to the Western Port side of the Peninsula, including unsealed roads and properties set back from the street. Add a note to your booking describing the gate, driveway or a nearby landmark, and mention if the vehicle can turn around on site. For wheelchair passengers, tell us where the most level spot for the ramp or hoist is.

faq.q: Do you do return trips from Bittern to Rosebud Hospital?
faq.a: We do. Rosebud Hospital is a common destination for Bittern residents, and we can book you there and back. If you are unsure when an appointment or discharge will finish, choose the pick up when ready option, then tap I'm ready or call us and we will send the nearest suitable vehicle, including a wheelchair accessible one.

name: Moorooduc
description: Moorooduc taxi and wheelchair taxi service for winery visits, farm properties and trips to Mornington and Frankston, available 24/7.
intro: Moorooduc is mostly open country, small farms and vineyards between Mornington and Somerville, and that is exactly where a reliable taxi earns its keep. Taxi Peninsula takes bookings for Moorooduc at any hour, with sedans for straightforward trips and wheelchair accessible vans and maxis for anyone who needs to stay in their chair.

The Moorooduc Highway runs through the district and Peninsula Link passes close by, so getting to Frankston or onto the freeway network is easy once you are in the car. The catch is that there is no regular train or much bus service here, and properties are spread out along roads such as Bungower Road and Derril Road. Locals call us to reach Mornington for shopping and medical appointments, Frankston Hospital, Frankston station, and the airport. Visitors often book us to move between cellar doors in Moorooduc and the nearby Red Hill and Main Ridge wine areas, so nobody has to drive after a tasting.

Because cars are not waiting on the street here, booking ahead makes a real difference, especially for early flights or a set appointment time. A group touring wineries can travel together in our Maxi WAT, which seats six plus two wheelchair positions. MPTP cards are accepted, as are NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers come along with the passenger. Ask for a fixed quote if you are planning a day out with several stops.
local: The Moorooduc Highway and Peninsula Link carry most traffic north towards Frankston, while Mornington-Tyabb Road crosses east to Tyabb and Hastings. Many properties sit behind farm gates or down long driveways, and mobile coverage can be patchy in pockets, so detailed pick-up notes help. Wineries and event venues get busy on weekends and during the summer holidays, and pick-ups at closing time are in demand. Book your return trip when you book the first leg so a car is lined up for the end of the day. Wedding and function venues in the district also generate late finishes, so give us the venue name and expected finishing time.

faq.q: Can I book a taxi for a day of winery visits from Moorooduc?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us the cellar doors you plan to visit and roughly when, and we can quote a fixed price for the day or book separate legs. Groups can share our Maxi WAT, which carries up to six seated passengers and two wheelchairs. Booking your return leg early is sensible because demand peaks when venues close on weekends.

faq.q: Is there public transport in Moorooduc?
faq.a: Public transport is very limited in Moorooduc, with no regular passenger train and sparse bus coverage across the farmland. Most residents without a car rely on taxis to reach Mornington, Frankston station or medical appointments. A standing booking for regular trips, such as weekly shopping or therapy sessions, saves you arranging each one separately.

faq.q: How do I make sure the driver finds my farm gate in Moorooduc?
faq.a: Use the notes field on the booking form to describe your gate, letterbox number, driveway length and any landmark on the road. If the driver should come up to the house, say so and mention whether the vehicle can turn around. For wheelchair passengers, a firm, level surface near the door makes loading by ramp or hoist easier.

name: Baxter
description: Baxter taxis and wheelchair accessible taxis, 24 hours a day. Rides to Frankston, Baxter station, hospitals and the airport.
intro: For Baxter residents, Taxi Peninsula is a local service rather than a city fleet that occasionally wanders this far south. We take bookings day and night, every day of the year, and we can send a sedan for an ordinary trip or a wheelchair accessible taxi with a ramp or hoist when that is what the passenger needs.

Baxter is a semi-rural community just south-east of Frankston, where Frankston-Flinders Road, Baxter-Tooradin Road and the Moorooduc Highway meet and Peninsula Link runs close by. Baxter station is on the Stony Point line, but trains run less often than on the metropolitan network, so a taxi to Frankston station is a popular choice for commuters and anyone with luggage. People here also travel regularly to Frankston Hospital, Bayside Shopping Centre, Monash University’s Peninsula campus and schools in the area, and out to Melbourne Airport or Avalon Airport for flights. Some families also book regular trips for children with additional needs, choosing the same vehicle type each time so the routine stays familiar.

Book the night before for early departures or a fixed appointment time so we can plan the car around you. If several people are travelling, or you have a heavier power chair, ask for the Maxi WAT, which takes two wheelchairs and six seated passengers.
