We accept MPTP cards and work with NDIS and aged-care accounts, and a carer can ride with the person they support at no fuss. The booking form shows a fare estimate before you confirm.
local: Baxter is where several busy routes converge, so school drop-off and pick-up times around the area can be slow, as can Frankston-Flinders Road heading into Frankston during the morning peak. Peninsula Link is close by and usually the quickest way north towards EastLink and the city. The Stony Point line stops at Baxter station; if you plan to change trains at Frankston, allow time for the connection. Many homes are on larger blocks, so mention a long driveway or shared access when booking. On rural edges of the suburb, gravel driveways and gates are common, and street lighting is limited at night.

faq.q: Is it quicker to take a taxi to Frankston station than the Stony Point train from Baxter?
faq.a: It often is, because Stony Point line services are less frequent than metropolitan trains and you still need to change at Frankston. A taxi takes you straight to the Frankston station forecourt to meet the train you want. For regular commutes, a recurring booking means you do not have to call each morning.

faq.q: Can you collect my child from school in the Baxter area?
faq.a: We can carry school-age passengers when a parent or guardian makes the booking and gives clear pick-up details, including the gate or meeting point. Let us know if a wheelchair accessible vehicle is needed. School finishing times are busy around Baxter, so booking ahead gives the driver the best chance of arriving right on time.

faq.q: Do you go from Baxter to Avalon Airport as well as Tullamarine?
faq.a: Yes, we take passengers from Baxter to both Melbourne Airport and Avalon Airport. Add your flight number when booking an airport pick-up and we track the flight, so the driver adjusts for early or late arrivals. For a departure, book the evening before and leave plenty of margin for check-in.

name: Langwarrin
description: Need a taxi in Langwarrin? Taxi Peninsula runs sedans and wheelchair taxis 24/7 to Frankston, Cranbourne, hospitals and the airport.
intro: Langwarrin is a big, spread-out suburb east of Frankston, and plenty of its households do not have a car for every trip. Taxi Peninsula fills that gap around the clock with sedans for regular rides and wheelchair accessible taxis for passengers using manual or power chairs. Many of our Langwarrin passengers are older residents and NDIS participants travelling to therapy, day programs and appointments, as well as commuters who simply want a reliable ride to the train.

Much of Langwarrin is family housing and bush-edged acreage, crossed by Cranbourne-Frankston Road, McClelland Drive and Peninsula Link, with Langwarrin South stretching towards Baxter and Pearcedale. There is no train station in the suburb, so a taxi to Frankston station is a common start to a trip into the city. Locals also travel to Frankston Hospital, Bayside Shopping Centre, Monash University’s Peninsula campus, and shopping and medical centres in Cranbourne. McClelland Sculpture Park and Gallery on McClelland Drive brings visitors into Langwarrin too, and the Langwarrin Flora and Fauna Reserve is a local landmark for walkers.

For early flights or appointments with a fixed start time, booking ahead is the surest way to have a car ready at your door. Families and small groups can travel together in the Maxi WAT, which seats six with room for two wheelchairs. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers accompany the passenger. Drivers help from door to door, which matters for older residents on sloping or bush blocks.
local: Cranbourne-Frankston Road is the main east-west route and is busy at peak times, particularly near the Peninsula Link interchange and approaching Frankston. Peninsula Link connects quickly north to EastLink and south towards the Peninsula. Langwarrin has no train line of its own; Frankston station on the Frankston line is the usual rail connection. Some Langwarrin South properties are on acreage with gates or unsealed driveways, so add directions to your booking. School zones slow traffic on weekday mornings and afternoons. Allow extra time on weekend afternoons, when traffic builds around shopping centres in Frankston and Cranbourne.

faq.q: Can you take me from Langwarrin to McClelland Sculpture Park and Gallery?
faq.a: Yes. McClelland is on McClelland Drive in Langwarrin and we can take you there and back from home or from Frankston station. We drop you at the gallery entrance area. Let us know if you need a wheelchair accessible vehicle, and consider booking your return trip with the pick up when ready option so you are not rushed.

faq.q: I live in Langwarrin South on acreage. Do you service those areas?
faq.a: We do. Langwarrin South properties can be well off the road, so please describe your gate, driveway and any turning area in the booking notes. If the driver should wait at the front gate instead, say so. For wheelchair passengers, mention where the ground is most level so the ramp or hoist can be set up safely.

faq.q: Do you travel from Langwarrin to Cranbourne for appointments?
faq.a: Yes. Many Langwarrin residents see doctors, specialists and services in Cranbourne as well as Frankston. Give us the clinic name and address when booking, along with your appointment time, and we will plan the pick-up to suit. A return trip can be booked at a set time or left open with the pick up when ready option.

name: Pearcedale
description: Pearcedale taxi and wheelchair accessible taxi bookings 24/7 for rides to Frankston, Cranbourne, Moonlit Sanctuary and the airport.
intro: Pearcedale is a semi-rural town on the eastern side of the Peninsula, close to Western Port, where distances are long and buses few. Taxi Peninsula covers Pearcedale 24 hours a day, sending a sedan for routine trips or a wheelchair accessible taxi when a passenger needs to travel in their chair. Many trips here are for medical appointments, shopping and getting to the train, because few residents live within walking distance of a bus.

The township is small, with a local shopping strip and a community feel, surrounded by hobby farms, horse properties and bushland. Baxter-Tooradin Road is the key route, linking Pearcedale to Baxter and Frankston in one direction and towards Tooradin and the South Gippsland Highway in the other. Moonlit Sanctuary Wildlife Conservation Park, a popular wildlife park, is on Tyabb Road in Pearcedale, and we often carry families and visitors there. Residents regularly book us for Frankston Hospital, Frankston station, Bayside Shopping Centre, Cranbourne for shopping and medical services, and Melbourne Airport.

Since Pearcedale has no train station and taxis are rarely passing, plan ahead: book early flights and medical appointments the day before. Larger households or groups can share our Maxi WAT, which fits six seated passengers and two wheelchairs, and it also handles heavier power chairs with its hydraulic hoist. MPTP cards are accepted, along with NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers travel with the passenger. The fare estimate on the booking form helps with budgeting longer trips.
local: Baxter-Tooradin Road carries most traffic in and out of Pearcedale and can be slow behind trucks and farm vehicles. Peninsula Link is reached via Baxter for quick trips north. There is no rail service in Pearcedale; Baxter and Somerville stations on the Stony Point line, or Frankston station, are the nearest. Many homes are on acreage with gates, animals or long driveways, so clear directions help the driver. Moonlit Sanctuary draws extra visitors on weekends and during school holidays. At night, many roads have little or no street lighting, so turning on a porch light or leaving the gate open helps the driver.

faq.q: Can you take our family from Pearcedale to Moonlit Sanctuary?
faq.a: Yes, Moonlit Sanctuary is on Tyabb Road in Pearcedale and we take locals and visitors there regularly, including guests staying elsewhere on the Peninsula. A family or small group can travel together in the Maxi WAT. If you are going to an evening session, book your return trip ahead so a car is ready when you finish.

faq.q: What is the nearest train station to Pearcedale?
faq.a: Pearcedale has no station of its own. The closest stops are Baxter and Somerville on the Stony Point line, while Frankston station gives direct access to the metropolitan Frankston line. Many residents take a taxi straight to Frankston to avoid changing trains. We can book a regular commute run if you travel on the same days each week.

faq.q: I have horses and gates at my Pearcedale property. How should I set up a booking?
faq.a: Add a note explaining which gate to use, whether it will be open, and if there are animals the driver should watch for. Tell us if the car should wait at the road. For wheelchair passengers, let us know where there is a firm surface for the ramp or hoist so loading is safe and comfortable.

name: Melbourne CBD
description: Taxi and wheelchair taxi from the Melbourne CBD to Frankston and the Mornington Peninsula, plus city hospitals, events and Southern Cross.
intro: Taxi Peninsula is based on the Mornington Peninsula, but a lot of our work begins in the Melbourne CBD. We bring people home from the city to Frankston, the Peninsula and the south-east at any hour, in sedans or in wheelchair accessible vehicles with ramps and hoists, so the trip back does not depend on finding a suitable car on a busy city street.

City trips usually start at a few familiar places. Southern Cross Station is the arrival point for regional and interstate coaches and V/Line trains, and Flinders Street Station is where the Frankston line begins. Melbourne’s major hospitals sit just outside the grid, including the Royal Melbourne Hospital, the Royal Women’s Hospital, the Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre and the Royal Children’s Hospital in Parkville, and the Royal Victorian Eye and Ear Hospital in East Melbourne. We also collect people after concerts, sport and conferences at the MCG, Rod Laver Arena, Marvel Stadium and the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre.

Pre-booking is the key in the city. Arrange a set time for a meeting or performance, or use the pick up when ready option after a hospital appointment or discharge, then tap I'm ready or call us when you are out. A group heading back to the Peninsula after a show can share the Maxi WAT, which seats six plus two wheelchairs. MPTP cards are accepted, NDIS and aged-care accounts are welcome, and carers travel with the passenger. Ask for a fixed quote for longer runs home.
local: Getting out of the city towards the south-east usually means Kings Way and the Monash Freeway, or the West Gate Freeway and CityLink, then EastLink and Peninsula Link down to the Peninsula. Peak hours and major events can slow these routes considerably. Many CBD streets have tram lanes, clearways and loading zones where stopping is restricted, so we agree a legal pick-up point in advance, such as a side street, a hotel drop-off area or a hospital patient pick-up zone. Large events at Melbourne Park and the MCG create heavy traffic around Olympic Boulevard and Punt Road.
nearby: Royal Victorian Eye and Ear Hospital

faq.q: Can you pick me up from a Parkville hospital and take me home to the Peninsula?
faq.a: Yes. We regularly collect patients from the Royal Melbourne, Royal Women’s, Peter Mac and Royal Children’s hospitals for the trip back to Frankston and the Peninsula. Choose the pick up when ready option if your discharge time is uncertain, then tap I'm ready or call us. Tell us the hospital and your ward or department when booking.

faq.q: Will you collect me after a game at the MCG or a concert at Rod Laver Arena?
faq.a: We can. Book in advance and nominate a pick-up point away from the main crowds, since the roads right beside the venues are often closed or jammed after events. We will confirm the spot by SMS or email. A group can share the Maxi WAT, and it also suits fans travelling with wheelchairs.

faq.q: I am arriving by V/Line or coach at Southern Cross. Can you meet me?
faq.a: Yes. Southern Cross Station is a common pick-up for passengers heading to Frankston and the Mornington Peninsula. Give us your expected arrival time and we will agree a meeting point outside the station. If your service is delayed, call us and we will adjust. Wheelchair accessible vehicles are available for passengers who travel in their chair.

name: Frankston
description: Frankston taxi and wheelchair accessible taxi service, 24/7. Trips to Frankston Hospital, the station, Bayside and Melbourne Airport.
intro: Frankston is the busiest part of our service area, and our drivers know its streets well. Taxi Peninsula operates here 24 hours a day, seven days a week, with sedans for quick local runs and a range of wheelchair accessible taxis for passengers who travel in a manual or power chair. Our passengers include hospital patients and visitors, students, commuters, shoppers and people heading home after a night out near the foreshore.

As the gateway to the Mornington Peninsula, Frankston has a lot going on. Frankston Hospital, the main public hospital run by Peninsula Health, is on Hastings Road and generates a steady flow of appointments, visits and discharges. Frankston station is the end of the metropolitan Frankston line and the start of the Stony Point line, while Bayside Shopping Centre, the Frankston Arts Centre and the foreshore near Frankston Pier draw people into the city centre. Monash University’s Peninsula campus and Chisholm Institute bring students, and the Nepean Highway, Frankston Freeway and Peninsula Link carry traffic in every direction.

For hospital discharges, the pick up when ready option means you are not stuck watching the clock: tap I'm ready or call us when you are cleared to go. Book ahead for early flights, day surgery and specialist appointments. Our Maxi WAT seats six and takes two wheelchairs, ideal for groups or heavier power chairs. We accept MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers travel with the passenger at no extra fuss.
local: Frankston’s centre can be congested around Nepean Highway, Young Street and the station precinct, especially at school times and on weekend afternoons. Frankston Hospital on Hastings Road is busy throughout the day, and drop-offs work best at the main entrance or the patient pick-up area; tell us your department. The Frankston line and Stony Point line meet at Frankston station. Summer events on the foreshore, such as the waterfront festivals, can close roads near the beach. Peninsula Link and the Frankston Freeway are the quickest routes north. Around Monash University’s Peninsula campus, class change times bring a lot of student traffic.

faq.q: Can I book a taxi home after being discharged from Frankston Hospital?
faq.a: Yes. Choose the pick up when ready option when you book, and once staff say you can leave, tap I'm ready or call us. We send the nearest suitable car, including a wheelchair accessible vehicle if needed. The driver meets you at the hospital entrance and can help with bags and getting settled at home.

faq.q: How do I get from Frankston to Melbourne Airport early in the morning?
faq.a: Book the night before and give us your flight time so we can plan the pick-up with plenty of margin. Early morning traffic is usually lighter, but we still allow for roadworks and freeway closures. For return trips, add your flight number and we track your arrival so the driver adjusts to delays.

faq.q: Do you pick up from Frankston station for people coming off the train?
faq.a: Yes, many passengers use us to finish a journey that started on the Frankston line or the Stony Point line. Tell us which side of the station you will exit and roughly when your train arrives. If you are travelling with a wheelchair, our ramp van or Maxi WAT can meet you at the station.

name: Mornington
description: Mornington taxi and wheelchair taxi bookings, day or night. Main Street, The Bays Hospital, the racecourse, Frankston and the airport.
intro: Mornington is one of the Peninsula’s main towns, and Taxi Peninsula serves it at every hour of the day and night. Whether you need a sedan for a quick hop to Main Street or a wheelchair accessible taxi with a rear ramp or hoist, we can send the right vehicle to your door. Locals use us for medical appointments, shopping and nights out, and visitors book us to move between accommodation, restaurants and wineries.

The heart of town is Main Street, with its cafes, shops and restaurants running down towards Mornington Pier and Mothers Beach. The Bays Hospital, a private hospital, is a common destination for appointments and surgery, and many residents also travel to Frankston Hospital. Mornington Racecourse hosts race meetings through the year, and the harbour and beaches draw crowds in summer. There has been no passenger train to Mornington for decades, so people heading to Melbourne often take a taxi to Frankston station or straight into the city. The Moorooduc Highway, Peninsula Link and the Nepean Highway link Mornington to the rest of the Peninsula.

For early flights, surgery admissions or specialist visits, book the day before so we can schedule your car. The Maxi WAT carries up to six seated passengers and two wheelchairs, which works for groups heading to dinner, a wedding or race day. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers ride with the passenger. If you would like certainty for a longer trip, ask for a fixed quote.
local: Main Street and the streets around the harbour get busy on weekends, during summer holidays and when markets or festivals are on, and parking turnover is slow. Choose a side-street pick-up if Main Street is crowded. Mornington has no train line, so Frankston station is the nearest rail link. The Moorooduc Highway and Peninsula Link carry most traffic towards Frankston and Melbourne, while the Nepean Highway runs along the coast to Mount Martha. Race days at Mornington Racecourse add traffic around the track. Much of the back of town is residential, with quieter streets that suit pick-ups and wheelchair loading.

faq.q: Can you take me to The Bays Hospital in Mornington for surgery and bring me home?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us your admission time when booking and we will plan the pick-up so you arrive with time to spare. For the trip home, use the pick up when ready option and tap I'm ready or call us once you are discharged. The driver can help you from the entrance to the car and into your home.

faq.q: Do you run taxis to and from Mornington Racecourse on race days?
faq.a: We do. Race days are busy, so book both legs in advance and agree a pick-up point away from the main gate queue. Groups can share our Maxi WAT, which seats six plus two wheelchair spaces. If your plans might change, keep your booking confirmation handy and call us to adjust the time.

faq.q: How do I get from Mornington to the city without a car?
faq.a: There is no train in Mornington, so most people take a taxi to Frankston station and continue on the Frankston line, or travel all the way into Melbourne by taxi. For hospital appointments in the city, a door-to-door trip often suits better. We can quote a fixed fare for a direct trip if you ask when booking.

name: Mount Martha
description: Mount Martha taxis and wheelchair accessible taxis, 24/7. Trips to the beaches, The Briars, Mornington, Frankston and airports.
intro: Mount Martha is a leafy coastal suburb, mostly homes on hilly streets above the bay, and its residents call Taxi Peninsula for trips large and small. We are available 24/7 with standard sedans and with wheelchair accessible vehicles that let passengers stay in their own chair.

The Esplanade follows the coastline past the bay beaches and beach boxes, while the Nepean Highway runs inland through the suburb. The Briars, a historic homestead and park with wetlands and walking trails, is a well-known local attraction, and the Balcombe Estuary reserve winds down to the bay. Mount Martha has a small village shopping area, so for larger shopping, appointments and hospital care people head to Mornington, The Bays Hospital, Frankston Hospital and Bayside Shopping Centre. There is no train station here, which makes a taxi to Frankston station the usual first step for city trips. The suburb also has a growing number of retirees, many of whom no longer drive at night and use taxis for dinners, concerts and family visits.

Many streets here are steep or winding and some driveways are tricky, so tell us about steps, slopes or limited turning space when you book. Book the evening before for early flights or appointments. Families and groups can use our Maxi WAT, with six seats plus two wheelchair positions. MPTP cards are accepted, along with NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers come along with the passenger. Drivers help door to door, including with bags and walking aids.
local: The Esplanade is scenic but narrow and slow in summer, when beachgoers park along both sides and pedestrians cross often. The Nepean Highway is usually the quicker route north to Mornington and south to Safety Beach and Dromana, with Peninsula Link reachable via the Mornington area. Hilly side streets and steep driveways can make kerbside pick-ups awkward, so a flatter meeting point may be better for wheelchair loading. There is no rail line; Frankston station is the nearest metropolitan connection. Beach box areas along the Esplanade have limited stopping space, so a car park entrance is usually a better meeting point.

faq.q: My Mount Martha home has a steep driveway. Can a wheelchair taxi still pick me up?
faq.a: Often yes, but it helps to tell us about the slope when booking. The driver will look for the safest level spot to deploy the ramp or hoist, which might be at the top or bottom of the driveway or on the street. If there is a flatter area nearby, mention it in the booking notes.

faq.q: Can you drop us at The Briars in Mount Martha?
faq.a: Yes. The Briars is on the Nepean Highway and we can take you there for a walk, an event or a visit to the homestead and bring you back later. Book your return at a set time, or use the pick up when ready option and let us know when you are finished.

faq.q: Is there a train from Mount Martha?
faq.a: No, Mount Martha has no train station. The nearest metropolitan rail is Frankston station on the Frankston line, which is why many residents book a taxi there before heading into the city. For hospital appointments or flights, a direct door-to-door trip is often less tiring than changing between car and train.

name: Mount Eliza
description: Mount Eliza taxi and wheelchair accessible taxi service available 24 hours, for school, station, hospital and airport trips.
intro: Tucked between Frankston and Mornington, Mount Eliza is a quiet, green suburb with a strong village centre, and Taxi Peninsula looks after its trips at any hour. Choose a sedan for an everyday ride or a wheelchair accessible taxi when a passenger needs ramp or hoist access. Older residents, school families and commuters all make up a large share of our bookings in the area.

Mount Eliza Village is the local hub for shopping, cafes and services, while the bayside streets of Ranelagh and the cliffs around Canadian Bay lead down to the water. Mount Eliza Regional Park sits on the inland side. The suburb is home to well-known schools such as Toorak College and Peninsula Grammar, so school-time trips are a regular part of our work. Nepean Highway and the Moorooduc Highway are the main roads, and with no train station in Mount Eliza, residents often book a taxi to Frankston station. Frankston Hospital, The Bays Hospital in Mornington and Bayside Shopping Centre are other common destinations.

If you are catching an early flight or have a fixed appointment time, book the night before. Our Maxi WAT seats six and carries two wheelchairs, and is handy for families, small groups or heavier power chairs. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and a carer can travel with the passenger. Fare estimates appear on the booking form, and fixed quotes are available on request.
local: Nepean Highway runs along the bay side of Mount Eliza and gets busy at school drop-off and pick-up times. The Moorooduc Highway, on the inland side, links quickly to Peninsula Link and Frankston. Mount Eliza Village can be congested on weekends, so a side-street pick-up may be faster. Some streets towards the bay are narrow and winding with steep driveways. The nearest rail link is Frankston station, where the Frankston line begins. Canadian Bay Road and the streets leading down to the bay have limited stopping space, so pick a driveway or side street for loading. Traffic towards Frankston can build on weekday mornings.

faq.q: Can you do regular trips to schools in Mount Eliza?
faq.a: Yes. Parents and guardians can set up recurring bookings for school runs to and from schools in Mount Eliza and nearby suburbs. Give us the student's details, the school gate or meeting point and the times. Let us know if a wheelchair accessible vehicle is needed. School zones are busy, so we plan pick-ups with a little margin.

faq.q: What is the easiest way from Mount Eliza to the train?
faq.a: Frankston station is the closest metropolitan station, and a taxi gets you there via the Nepean or Moorooduc Highway. Tell us which train you are aiming for so we can time the pick-up. For daily commuters, a standing booking saves calling each morning, and you will get confirmation by SMS or email.

faq.q: Can a wheelchair taxi pick me up from Mount Eliza Village?
faq.a: Yes. The village can be busy, so we usually suggest a quieter side street or a spot with enough room behind the vehicle for the ramp or hoist. Describe where you will be waiting in the booking notes, and the driver will come to you and help with loading and restraints.

name: Dromana
description: Dromana taxi and wheelchair taxi service, 24/7. Rides to Arthurs Seat, the foreshore, Rosebud Hospital, Frankston and the airport.
intro: Dromana sits at the foot of Arthurs Seat where the Peninsula’s bay coast begins to curve west, and Taxi Peninsula is on call here day and night. We send sedans for regular trips and wheelchair accessible taxis for passengers who need to stay seated in their chair. Our passengers range from permanent residents heading to appointments to holidaymakers staying in foreshore cabins and caravans.

Point Nepean Road is the town’s main street, lined with shops and cafes facing the foreshore and Dromana Pier. Behind the town, Arthurs Seat rises steeply, with the Arthurs Seat Eagle gondola and the state park lookouts drawing visitors year round. The Dromana Drive-in remains a local favourite on summer evenings, and the foreshore camping grounds fill up during holidays. Red Hill and its wineries are just up the hill, while the Mornington Peninsula Freeway gives fast access north towards Peninsula Link. Locals travel to Rosebud Hospital, Frankston Hospital, shopping in Rosebud and Mornington, and the airports.

During the summer peak, Point Nepean Road slows to a crawl, so pre-book trips that cannot be late. For early flights, book the evening before. Groups of friends heading to a winery lunch can share the Maxi WAT, which seats six plus two wheelchair spaces. We take MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers travel with the passenger. Ask for a fixed quote for longer journeys, such as a trip to Melbourne Airport or the city.
local: Point Nepean Road through Dromana carries heavy holiday traffic in summer, with camping grounds and beach parking along the foreshore. The Mornington Peninsula Freeway bypasses the town and is usually faster for trips north to Frankston and Melbourne. Arthurs Seat Road is steep and winding, so allow extra time and expect slow vehicles. Pick-ups at the foreshore are easiest at a defined spot such as a car park entry or the pier area. There is no train line on this side of the Peninsula. Off-season, the town is far quieter and pick-ups along the main street are straightforward.

faq.q: Can you take us up Arthurs Seat from Dromana?
faq.a: Yes. We can drop you at the Arthurs Seat Eagle base station or at the summit area, and pick you up again later. The road is steep and winding, so we plan a little extra time. If someone in your group uses a wheelchair, our accessible vehicles can do the trip comfortably.

faq.q: Do you pick up from the Dromana foreshore camping grounds?
faq.a: We do. Give us your site area or a clear meeting point such as the camping ground entrance, because foreshore grounds can be crowded in summer and site numbers are hard to find at night. Mention any luggage or eskies so we send a vehicle with enough room.

faq.q: Is it worth booking ahead for a winery trip from Dromana to Red Hill?
faq.a: It is, particularly on weekends and in summer when cellar doors and restaurants are busy and cars are in high demand. Book both legs at once so your ride home is secured. Groups can share the Maxi WAT, which takes six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs.

name: Rosebud
description: Rosebud taxi and wheelchair accessible taxi, open 24/7. Trips to Rosebud Hospital, the foreshore, Rosebud Plaza and Frankston.
intro: Rosebud is the largest town on the southern Peninsula, and a lot of our bookings start or finish here. Taxi Peninsula runs around the clock in Rosebud, with sedans for everyday trips and wheelchair accessible taxis fitted with ramps or hoists for passengers who need them.

Rosebud Hospital, part of Peninsula Health, is on Point Nepean Road and is a frequent pick-up and drop-off point for appointments, emergency visits and discharges. Rosebud Plaza is the main shopping centre, and the strip along Point Nepean Road has banks, chemists and cafes facing the foreshore and Rosebud Pier. In summer the foreshore camping grounds fill with holidaymakers and the town becomes much busier. Residents also travel to Frankston Hospital for specialist care, to Mornington and Frankston for shopping and to Melbourne Airport. Boneo Road and Jetty Road connect the town to the Mornington Peninsula Freeway. Outside the holiday season Rosebud is a settled community with many retirees, which is why medical and shopping trips make up much of our weekday work.

After a stay at Rosebud Hospital, book with the pick up when ready option and tap I'm ready or call us when you are cleared to leave. For early flights or day procedures, book the night before. Our Maxi WAT carries six seated passengers and two wheelchairs. MPTP cards are accepted, and we work with NDIS and aged-care accounts; carers travel with the passenger. Drivers help from door to door.
local: Point Nepean Road is the main street and gets heavily congested in the summer holidays, especially near the foreshore camping areas and the plaza. Boneo Road and Jetty Road lead up to the Mornington Peninsula Freeway, which is the faster way towards Frankston. There is no train line on the southern Peninsula. Rosebud Hospital sits right on Point Nepean Road, and patient pick-ups work best at the main entrance; let us know your department. Plaza car parks are busy on weekends. Off-season, traffic is much lighter, and most of our trips are local errands and medical appointments.

faq.q: Can you take me home from Rosebud Hospital?
faq.a: Yes. Rosebud Hospital is one of our most common pick-ups. Choose the pick up when ready option when booking and tap I'm ready or call when you are discharged. The driver will meet you at the entrance and can help with bags and walking aids, and a wheelchair accessible vehicle can be sent if you need one.

faq.q: Do you service the Rosebud foreshore during the summer holidays?
faq.a: We do, though summer traffic along Point Nepean Road is heavy, so book ahead for anything time-sensitive. Give us your camping ground and a clear meeting point, such as the entrance off the main road. Late-night trips home from dinner or the pub are popular, so a pre-booked return trip is a good idea.

faq.q: How do I get from Rosebud to Frankston Hospital for a specialist appointment?
faq.a: We take Rosebud residents to Frankston Hospital regularly, usually via the Mornington Peninsula Freeway and Peninsula Link. Book a pick-up time that leaves room for traffic and finding your clinic. For the return, a set time or the pick up when ready option both work, depending on how predictable your appointment is.

name: Rye
description: Rye taxi and wheelchair taxi bookings at any hour, for the foreshore, back beaches, Peninsula Hot Springs and Rosebud Hospital.
intro: Rye is a relaxed seaside town on the southern Peninsula, quiet in winter and lively in summer, and Taxi Peninsula covers it at all hours of the day and night. We send a sedan for ordinary trips and a wheelchair accessible taxi whenever a passenger needs ramp or hoist access.

On the bay side, Rye’s main shopping strip faces the foreshore along Point Nepean Road, close to Rye Pier and its calm beach. A short drive south takes you across the Peninsula to the rugged ocean back beaches, including St Andrews Beach and Gunnamatta. Peninsula Hot Springs in nearby Fingal attracts visitors throughout the year, and local golf courses are popular too. Residents commonly travel to Rosebud Hospital, Rosebud Plaza, Sorrento for the ferry, Frankston Hospital and Melbourne Airport, and holidaymakers book us to and from rental houses in summer. Outside summer, Rye is a settled community with many retirees and families who live here year round, and their trips tend to be medical appointments, shopping in Rosebud and visits to family.

Taxis are spread more thinly at the bottom of the Peninsula, so booking ahead is especially worthwhile for early flights or appointments in Frankston and Melbourne. Families and groups can share the Maxi WAT, which takes six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers travel with the passenger. A fixed quote can be arranged for longer trips.
local: Point Nepean Road through Rye is slow in summer, with foreshore camping, beach parking and pedestrians crossing to the beach. The Mornington Peninsula Freeway ends near Rosebud, so trips north follow local roads towards Rosebud before joining it. Roads to the ocean beaches are narrow and can have sandy verges, and some holiday streets are unsealed. There is no train service here. When booking a holiday rental pick-up, include the full address and any name on the property, as numbering can be hard to spot at night. On ocean beach days, car parks at the back beaches fill early and stopping space near the paths is limited.

faq.q: Can you take us from Rye to Peninsula Hot Springs?
faq.a: Yes. Peninsula Hot Springs is in Fingal, close to Rye, and we take visitors there often. Book your return trip in advance or use the pick up when ready option, because demand rises in the evenings. Wheelchair accessible vehicles are available, and groups can travel together in the Maxi WAT.

faq.q: I am staying in a holiday rental in Rye. How do I make a booking?
faq.a: Book online or by phone with the full street address, plus any property name or description that helps the driver find it at night. Rye holiday streets can be dark and poorly numbered. Add your mobile number so the driver can reach you, and your confirmation will arrive by SMS or email.

faq.q: Do you go from Rye to the ocean back beaches?
faq.a: We do. We can drop you at back beach car parks such as St Andrews Beach and pick you up later. Mobile reception can be patchy near some ocean beaches, so it is best to book your return at a set time. Note that the paths down to the sand are often steep and not suited to wheelchairs.

name: Sorrento
description: Sorrento taxi and wheelchair accessible taxi, 24/7. Rides to the Queenscliff ferry, back beach, Rosebud Hospital and Melbourne Airport.
intro: Near the tip of the Peninsula, Sorrento is a historic seaside village with a busy summer season and a steady local community, and Taxi Peninsula serves it every hour of every day. Sedans handle everyday trips, and our wheelchair accessible taxis carry passengers in their own chairs.

Ocean Beach Road is Sorrento’s main street, lined with limestone buildings, galleries, cafes and boutiques running up from the bay. At the foreshore, the Searoad ferry crosses Port Phillip to Queenscliff on the Bellarine Peninsula, and many of our passengers arrive or depart that way. Sorrento Back Beach and its rock pools face Bass Strait on the other side of the narrow Peninsula, and Point Nepean National Park begins just beyond Portsea. Locals rely on us for trips to Rosebud Hospital, Rosebud Plaza, Frankston Hospital, and Melbourne and Avalon airports, while visitors book us for restaurants, weddings and holiday accommodation. Out of season the town is quieter, and permanent residents use us for regular shopping trips, medical appointments and visits to family.

At the far end of the Peninsula, pre-booking is the best way to secure a car, particularly for early flights, ferry connections and evenings in summer. Groups heading to a wedding or dinner can share our Maxi WAT, which seats six plus two wheelchairs. MPTP cards are accepted and NDIS and aged-care accounts are welcome, with carers travelling alongside the passenger. Ask about a fixed quote for airport runs.
local: Ocean Beach Road and the foreshore around the ferry terminal are very busy in summer and on long weekends, and parking is scarce. Point Nepean Road is the only main road in and out, so expect slow traffic during holiday peaks and after events. Ferry arrivals bring a rush of passengers at once, so arrange a clear meeting point near the terminal. There is no train on the southern Peninsula. Many back-street holiday homes are hard to find at night, so add property details to your booking. Narrow side streets near the main street have limited stopping space.

faq.q: Can you meet me off the Queenscliff ferry in Sorrento?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us roughly which sailing you are on and we will arrange a meeting point near the Sorrento ferry terminal. If the crossing is delayed, call us and we will adjust. Foot passengers with luggage, and passengers travelling in a wheelchair, can be met with a suitable vehicle.

faq.q: Do you take wedding guests from Sorrento venues back to their accommodation?
faq.a: We do. Book in advance with the venue name, finish time and the addresses guests need to reach. Late evenings in summer are busy, so locking in times early is wise. Our Maxi WAT can carry six seated guests plus two wheelchairs, which is useful for families or older relatives.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book an airport taxi from Sorrento?
faq.a: Book at least the day before, and earlier during summer and holiday periods. Sorrento is at the far end of the Peninsula, so we plan the pick-up time carefully around your flight. For arrivals, include your flight number and we will track it so the driver is there when you land.

name: Portsea
description: Taxi and wheelchair taxi service in Portsea, around the clock. Trips to Point Nepean National Park, the Portsea Hotel and the airport.
intro: Portsea is the last township on the Mornington Peninsula, a small, affluent seaside village set between Port Phillip and Bass Strait. Taxi Peninsula reaches it 24 hours a day with sedans and with wheelchair accessible vehicles for passengers who need to travel in their chair.

The village centres on the Portsea Hotel and the foreshore near Portsea Pier, which is busy with swimmers, divers and boaties in the warmer months. Beyond the township, Point Nepean National Park stretches to the tip of the Peninsula, with the historic Quarantine Station, Fort Nepean and coastal walking tracks. Portsea Back Beach and the London Bridge rock formation are on the ocean side. With few services in Portsea itself, residents and guests travel to Sorrento for shops and cafes, Rosebud Hospital and Rosebud Plaza, Frankston Hospital, and Melbourne Airport. Many homes here are holiday houses, so our bookings range from permanent residents needing appointments to guests arriving for summer stays, weddings and long lunches.

Pre-booking matters at the far tip of the Peninsula, so arrange early-morning airport runs the day before and book summer evening returns well ahead. For a group lunch or wedding, the Maxi WAT seats six with room for two wheelchairs. We accept MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers ride with the passenger. Ask for a fixed quote on a long trip back to Melbourne, and add your flight number for airport pick-ups.
local: Point Nepean Road ends at Portsea, so every trip in or out follows the same route through Sorrento, which slows considerably in summer and on long weekends. The Portsea Hotel and foreshore get crowded on warm afternoons, and kerbside space is tight. Inside Point Nepean National Park, roads and visitor areas have their own access arrangements, so we drop off and collect at the main visitor area unless you tell us otherwise. Mobile coverage can be patchy on the ocean side. There is no train service. Many holiday homes sit on private roads or behind gates and dense tea-tree, so please give the driver clear directions and a contact number in your booking.

faq.q: Can you take us to Point Nepean National Park from Portsea?
faq.a: Yes. We usually drop off at the main visitor area near the park entrance, where the Quarantine Station precinct is. Let us know if you would like to be collected later, and book a set time since mobile reception can be unreliable in parts of the park. Accessible vehicles are available for wheelchair users.

faq.q: Will you pick up from the Portsea Hotel late at night?
faq.a: We can. Summer evenings at the Portsea Hotel are busy, so book your trip home in advance and agree a pick-up point out of the main crowd. Groups heading back to Sorrento, Rye or further can share the Maxi WAT, which seats six plus two wheelchairs.

faq.q: How do I get from Portsea to Melbourne Airport?
faq.a: Book a taxi at least a day ahead and give us your flight time, so we can plan a pick-up that allows for traffic along Point Nepean Road and the freeways. For the trip home, add your flight number and we will track it. A fixed quote is available on request for this longer journey.

name: Hastings
description: Hastings taxi and wheelchair accessible taxi service, 24/7, for the station, marina, HMAS Cerberus, Frankston Hospital and beyond.
intro: Hastings is the main town on the Western Port side of the Peninsula, a working port and marina community, and Taxi Peninsula covers it every hour of the week. We dispatch sedans for everyday travel and wheelchair accessible taxis for passengers who stay in their chair for the journey. Our passengers include residents travelling to appointments and shopping, marina visitors, and people working in and around the port.

The town centre sits around High Street and the Frankston-Flinders Road, with shops, a supermarket and medical services. Down at the water, the Hastings foreshore, Western Port Marina and the fishing jetties are popular with boating families and anglers, and the Port of Hastings brings industry and shift work. Hastings station is on the Stony Point line, with less frequent trains than the metropolitan network, so many people prefer a taxi to Frankston station. HMAS Cerberus at Crib Point is close by, and we often carry navy personnel and visiting families. Frankston Hospital, Rosebud Hospital, Bayside Shopping Centre and Melbourne Airport are regular destinations.

Shift workers and early travellers should book the night before so a car is ready on time. For groups, or a heavier power chair, the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist and seats six plus two wheelchairs. We take MPTP cards, and NDIS and aged-care accounts; carers travel with the passenger. The fare estimate shows before you confirm, and fixed quotes are available.
local: Frankston-Flinders Road is the main route north through Tyabb and Somerville to Frankston, and it can slow at school and work start times. The Stony Point line stops at Hastings station, but trains are infrequent. Around the marina and foreshore, weekend boat traffic and trailer parking can make pick-ups tricky, so choose a clear meeting point. For HMAS Cerberus, we drop off at the main gate area unless you have other arrangements. Many residential streets are quiet and wide, making wheelchair loading straightforward at the kerb. On summer weekends, traffic builds near the foreshore and boat ramps.

faq.q: Can you take me from Hastings to HMAS Cerberus?
faq.a: Yes. HMAS Cerberus is at Crib Point, a short trip from Hastings, and we carry personnel, visitors and families there regularly. We drop off at the main gate area, as access beyond that depends on base security arrangements. Book ahead for early starts and for ceremonies or family days, when traffic around the base increases.

faq.q: Is the Stony Point train or a taxi better for getting from Hastings to Frankston?
faq.a: It depends on timing. The Stony Point line runs less often than metropolitan trains, so if your schedule does not match, a taxi to Frankston station or Frankston Hospital is quicker. A taxi is also easier with luggage, shopping or a wheelchair. We can set up regular bookings for commuting.

faq.q: Do you pick up shift workers in Hastings at night?
faq.a: We do. Taxi Peninsula runs 24 hours, seven days, and shift workers in Hastings and around the port book us for late finishes and early starts. Set up a recurring booking so you do not have to arrange each trip, and include the exact gate or meeting point at your workplace.

name: Somerville
description: Somerville taxi and wheelchair taxi, available 24/7. Trips to Somerville and Frankston stations, hospitals, shops and airports.
intro: Somerville is a growing town on the eastern side of the Peninsula, with new estates spreading out from an established centre, and Taxi Peninsula serves it around the clock. You can book a sedan for ordinary journeys or a wheelchair accessible taxi with a ramp or hydraulic hoist. Young families, older residents in established streets and commuters heading for the train all use us, and we are glad to set up regular bookings for appointments and therapy.

The town centre is along Eramosa Road, with supermarkets, cafes and local services, and Frankston-Flinders Road runs through on its way between Baxter and Tyabb. Somerville station is on the Stony Point line, and Somerville Secondary College and several primary schools make school times busy. Locals travel to Frankston Hospital, Frankston station for metropolitan trains, Bayside Shopping Centre, Mornington for shops and The Bays Hospital, and Melbourne Airport. The town is surrounded by orchards, nurseries and small farms, so some addresses are well out of the centre.

Book the night before if you have an early flight or a set appointment time. The Maxi WAT seats six with two wheelchair positions, ideal for family groups or heavier power chairs. We accept MPTP cards, along with NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers travel with the passenger. Drivers help from the door to the vehicle, including with walking frames and shopping bags, and you will receive confirmation by SMS or email.
local: Eramosa Road and Frankston-Flinders Road meet in the town centre and can be busy at school drop-off and pick-up times. Peninsula Link is accessible via Baxter for faster trips north to EastLink and Melbourne. Somerville station is on the Stony Point line; trains are less frequent than metropolitan services, so check connections at Frankston. Newer estates have similar-looking streets, so double-check the address when booking, and farm properties should include gate details. Outside the centre, rural roads have little street lighting, so a porch light helps at night. Weekend traffic towards Hastings and the Western Port coast also passes through town.

faq.q: Can you take me from Somerville station to home with my shopping?
faq.a: Yes, and the driver can help carry bags to your door. Many Somerville residents use a taxi between the station, the Eramosa Road shops and home. If you need a wheelchair accessible vehicle, tell us when booking, and give a clear pick-up point near the station or the shops.

faq.q: Do you go from Somerville to Mornington for appointments?
faq.a: We do. Mornington is a common destination for Somerville residents, whether for The Bays Hospital, specialists or shopping. Give us the clinic name and appointment time, and choose a set return time or the pick up when ready option. A carer can travel with the passenger.

faq.q: My Somerville address is in a new estate. Will the driver find it?
faq.a: New streets sometimes take time to show up in maps. Add a note with the nearest main road or a landmark, and check your street name and number when booking. If the estate has several entrances, mention which one to use. Your confirmation by SMS or email shows the address for checking.

name: Tyabb
description: Tyabb taxi and wheelchair taxi bookings, 24 hours a day. Rides to the Packing House, Tyabb station, Frankston and Hastings.
intro: Tyabb is a small rural township between Somerville and Hastings, known for orchards, antiques and its airfield, and Taxi Peninsula is available here 24 hours a day. We offer sedans for everyday trips and wheelchair accessible taxis for passengers who use a manual or power chair.

The Tyabb Packing House Antique Centre, in an old fruit packing shed on Mornington-Tyabb Road, attracts collectors and day-trippers, and the nearby antiques and homewares stores make it a popular stop. Tyabb Airfield, a small general aviation airfield, is also in the area. Tyabb station is on the Stony Point line, while the Frankston-Flinders Road connects north to Somerville and Frankston and south to Hastings. Residents rely on taxis for Frankston Hospital, Frankston station, shopping in Hastings and Mornington, and trips to Melbourne Airport, since bus services are limited. The surrounding countryside is dotted with orchards, horse properties and small farms, and some families have lived in the district for generations. Many older residents no longer drive, so a dependable taxi for appointments and shopping makes a real difference.

With properties spread across farmland, it pays to book ahead, especially for early flights and medical appointments. Group visits to the antiques district can travel in the Maxi WAT, which seats six with two wheelchair spaces. We accept MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers come with the passenger. Fare estimates are shown on the booking form.
local: Frankston-Flinders Road and Mornington-Tyabb Road are the main roads in Tyabb; both carry trucks and farm machinery, which can slow traffic. The Stony Point line stops at Tyabb station, but services are infrequent. Many homes are on farmland with gates and long driveways, so include directions and mention whether the gate will be open. Weekend visitors to the antique centre add traffic around the Mornington-Tyabb Road area. There is little street lighting on rural roads, so a porch light or open gate helps at night. If you are visiting the antiques district, agree a pick-up point in a car park rather than on the roadside, where stopping is difficult.

faq.q: Can you take a group to the antique shops in Tyabb?
faq.a: Yes. The Tyabb Packing House Antique Centre is a popular day out, and we can bring a group from anywhere on the Peninsula or Frankston. The Maxi WAT seats six plus two wheelchairs. Small purchases fit easily, but please tell us in advance if you plan to bring home larger items.

faq.q: Is there a train from Tyabb to Frankston?
faq.a: Yes, Tyabb station is on the Stony Point line, which runs to Frankston. Services are less frequent than metropolitan trains, so many locals take a taxi to Frankston station or straight to their appointment instead. We can book a regular commute if you travel on the same days.

faq.q: I live on a farm property near Tyabb. What details should I give?
faq.a: Provide the full address, the gate or entrance to use, whether it will be open and how far the house is from the road. Mention animals, cattle grids or a turning area. For wheelchair passengers, tell us where the ground is firm and level for the ramp or hoist.

name: Carrum Downs
description: Carrum Downs taxi and wheelchair accessible taxi service, 24/7, for workplaces, Frankston Hospital, stations, shops and airports.
intro: Carrum Downs mixes residential streets with a large industrial area, and Taxi Peninsula serves both day and night. We send sedans for regular trips and wheelchair accessible taxis for people who need to travel in their chair.

The suburb sits between the Frankston Freeway, EastLink and the Frankston-Dandenong Road, which makes it a key junction for trips around the south-east. Its industrial estates around roads like Hall Road and Ballarto Road employ many shift workers, while the residential side has shops, schools and aged-care facilities. There is no train station in the suburb; the nearest are Seaford, Kananook and Frankston on the Frankston line. People commonly travel to Frankston Hospital, Bayside Shopping Centre, Dandenong, Monash Medical Centre and Melbourne Airport. Residents use us to get to work, appointments, the shops and the train, and also for social trips such as family visits or nights out in Frankston. We also carry workers between sites and to the airport for business travel.

If you work early or late shifts, a recurring booking takes the hassle out of getting to work. Book ahead for flights and medical appointments too, especially on weekday mornings when the freeways are busy. Our Maxi WAT carries six seated passengers and two wheelchairs, useful for groups, work teams or aged-care outings.
